/projection_pages/Operating-Houses.md/in.en: The houses of 2126 stood in two lines. The corporate heirs were grandchildren of the hands that had held the keys of the 2026 owners' families. The civic houses had grown out of watches at the water gates, the records, and the medicine. They did not buy states. They leased the infrastructure. Before a station chief could open the water, a house's signature was required. The founding owners' faces lived on as oral accounts. Heo Eunchan and Yu Sejin belonged to the generation of 2126. The causes sat with [the houses](./factions/Chaebol-Houses-and-Century-Factions.md).

/projection_pages/External-Theaters.md/b.en: The corridor prose of this page was a read-only projection of the World Narrative Atlas.

/houses/24/arcs/0/summary.en: the Suseo protection-treaty violation record disappeared from the Sangam tower index

/houses/24/arcs/1/summary.en: Ryu Gaon staked the same rebuttal time for the Magok verifier and the advertisement-slot buyer

/houses/24/arcs/2/summary.en: after the award ledger was published, the Digital Media City Index House lost its most expensive advertisement slot

/houses/24/prose.en:
Beneath the Sangam transmission tower, the Digital Media City Index House bound severed documents and broadcasts into a single search index.

Each rumor carried a verification table and a counter-argument timestamp, so that verdicts themselves could not be traded.

Ryu Gaon published the Suseo contract ledgers side by side with the advertisement-slot bidding records.

The Magok researchers appended to the earlier verdicts whenever the evidence changed, and never erased them.

Even when buyers paid for ranking, they could not touch the evidence lines under the search results.

When the protection-treaty violation record vanished, the index keeper and the auction observer each opened a different vault.

Instead of exposing the manipulation, the Digital Media City Index House gave up its largest advertisement slot and its southern passage rights.

/houses/25/arcs/0/summary.en: the warehouse switchboard went dark, and the Sinnae medical-train call could not reach Sangam

/houses/25/arcs/1/summary.en: Pyo Yunjae cut the freight dispatch circuits and spliced a temporary relay onto the railway roof

/houses/25/arcs/2/summary.en: the price of saving the medical calls was one bay of the exchange, ceded to the Yongsan track house

/houses/25/prose.en:
In the Yongsan rail warehouse, the switchboard of the Yongsan Exchange House carried words between Sangam and Sinnae.

The trackside base station borrowed freight-truck batteries to keep a short relay stretch alive.

Users of the leased lines were set not by the track houses but by call order.

On the exchange board Pyo Yunjae kept, dispatch orders and medical requests were logged under different indexes.

When a downpour snapped the rooftop relay, the Sinnae patient-transport signal was the first to move onto the detour line.

The freight merchants demanded a dedicated line to cover their losses, and the subscribers' delegate blocked it.

As the price of the revived route, KT handed over the operating rights to one bay of the Yongsan exchange room.

/houses/26/arcs/0/summary.en: an electrolyte drum in the Guro–Geumcheon stockpile leaked, and even the Ttukseom certificates came under doubt

/houses/26/arcs/1/summary.en: Bae Haesol sealed the Changdong braking-battery share and fought the production-alliance repair crews over the retesting order

/houses/26/arcs/2/summary.en: the contaminated bundles were discarded whole, and one reserve run of the northern trains was given up

/houses/26/prose.en:
Along the Guro–Geumcheon production axis, the Guro Digital Complex Battery House sorted loose battery cells into stacks by lifespan and temperature.

The Ttukseom workshop took sealed electrolyte drums and built power bundles for pumps and small machines.

The Changdong rolling-stock depot demanded its braking stock first, and accepted no material without a test certificate.

Bae Haesol's seal guaranteed not charge capacity but heat-resistance testing and contamination history.

When one leaking drum was found, every bundle on the same freight cart went into quarantine.

The production repair crews pressed for the shortage to be released, and the northern technicians blocked the warehouse door to hold the braking share.

After the materials certifier uncovered forged markings, the supply order changed to an open draw among three states.

To keep its trust, the Guro Digital Complex Battery House discarded even usable cells and cut Changdong's reserve runs.

/houses/27/arcs/0/summary.en: a ship grounded under the Han River bridges jammed the Yongsan riverside logistics and the barge routes at once

/houses/27/arcs/1/summary.en: Cha Yunho opened wharf negotiations that tied the Noryangjin cold freight to Garak auction access

/houses/27/arcs/2/summary.en: the exclusive wharf was given up, and one berth ledger covered every sealed consignment

/houses/27/prose.en:
Under the rusted cranes of the Yongsan north bank, HMM assigned the barge berths.

Cha Yunho logged the Han River bridge crossing times alongside the rail dispatch table.

A cold box loaded at Noryangjin reached the Garak wholesale auction floor only with its seal tag intact.

The old air-cargo standard survived as a ledger rule separating weight from liability for damage.

The shipowners demanded faster routes, and the landing inspectors confirmed the priority of public freight.

When a grounded ship blocked the channel, three states each pressed their wharf rights.

HMM gave up its exclusive berth and, in exchange, published every stevedoring fee and sailing order.

/houses/28/arcs/0/summary.en: ahead of the Seoul Station protocol talks, the banquet-goods delivery tags vanished from the Garak auction

/houses/28/arcs/1/summary.en: before the Suseo contract auditor, Seo Haejin exposed the hidden guarantor behind the room assignments and the banquet credit

/houses/28/arcs/2/summary.en: the privileged guests' bonded warehouse was opened, and famine rations were parted from diplomatic return gifts

/houses/28/prose.en:
Along the protocol road at Seoul Station stood the neutral guest lodges kept by the Dongdaeipgu Trading House.

An envoy who had surrendered weapons was still not detained over lodging debts.

Banquet goods were bought at open auction in the Garak wholesale market and tagged item by item.

Seo Haejin handed the Suseo contract auditor the room ledger and the banquet credit ledger together.

The old bonded warehouse filled less with splendid goods than with handicrafts owed as treaty gifts.

On short rations the banquet tables thinned first, and the ordinary guests' porridge stayed as it was.

When a hidden guarantor came to light, the guest-observer cancelled the trade regardless of protocol rank.

/houses/29/arcs/0/summary.en: one Seoul Station protocol performance was struck from the tower's prime-time schedule

/houses/29/arcs/1/summary.en: as forged tickets spread through the Garak assembly ground, Baek Sowon set the performance-rights ledger against the broadcast records

/houses/29/arcs/2/summary.en: the exclusive performance rights were loosed for a moment, and every state's testimony went out in the same broadcast hours

/houses/29/prose.en:
Every evening the Sangam transmission tower lit, HYBE sealed the performance order.

Baek Sowon entered the rights to a song and the price of a broadcast slot in different ledgers.

A performer who took the Seoul Station protocol stage had name and return passage guaranteed under the records office's accreditation.

At the Garak assembly ground, every three paid tickets left one refugee seat open.

When the channel guild pushed popularity rankings alone, the audience observer suspended the programming meeting.

The forged-ticket uproar shook not only the ticket revenue but the tower's verification trust as well.

HYBE divided the final broadcast hours among the states' testimonies and published the release of its exclusive rights.

/houses/30/arcs/0/summary.en: ledger sync with Suseo broke, and the transfer calls piled up

/houses/30/arcs/1/summary.en: Sim Haru negotiated a split of the lines between Sangam transmission verification and Sinnae transfer neutrality

/houses/30/arcs/2/summary.en: the message relay was cut back, but the payment ledger survived whole

/houses/30/prose.en:
From the basement relay room of an old Sangam office block, the Digital Media City Payments House kept the transfer-payment lines.

Sim Haru bound the message queues and the payment ledgers into separate capacitor banks.

When the Suseo charter city demanded notarized ledgers, he opened audit read-access alone and never handed over the signing key.

The Neutral Convoy City's call window was fenced with queue rules so that no faction's troops could jump the line.

Even with the lines dead, the last settlement block stayed on paper.

/houses/31/arcs/0/summary.en: the residual lost-line signal beneath the Magok test line rose again

/houses/31/arcs/1/summary.en: Baek Seonwoo split the drawing key between the Magok council and the Sangam works

/houses/31/arcs/2/summary.en: the test line went back under lock, and only the charging standard remained

/houses/31/prose.en:
Beside the autonomous test line at the edge of the Magok research grounds, the Magok Test-Line House kept the energy-storage depot.

Baek Seonwoo tended the pre-collapse charging connectors and the test-line breakers together.

When the old insect-, dinosaur-, and deep-form test units woke on their own beneath the line, only half of the drawing key came out, under the watch of the Magok council.

When the Changdong depot's charging circuits turned unstable, he closed the certification for a while and settled the circuits first.

Even with the depot empty, the certification seal was never forged.

/theaters/0/verified.en: Only the public geographic positions of the Imjin–Han confluence and the northern transfer and refugee corridors were used as fact anchors. No crimes or policy claims of current regimes or sitting institutions were recorded.

/theaters/0/inference.en: Only the inference was allowed that post-collapse flows of goods and refugees toward Kaesong and Pyongyang saw repeated severance and detour, and it was not promoted to canon.

/theaters/0/original_fiction.en: The Imjin River Gate Theater was a Seoul creative corridor in which Anguk, Gwanghwamun, Sinnae, and Guui jointly ran the gate quarantine and the repatriation registers.

/theaters/0/scenario_chains/0/summary.en: At the Imjin provisional quarantine post the repatriation register is damaged and Jogyesa at Anguk demands reissue

/theaters/0/scenario_chains/1/summary.en: After the Gangnam group's escort stops outside the gate, Sinnae opens a detour transfer

/theaters/0/scenario_chains/2/summary.en: The Gwanghwamun complex screens forged kinship certificates and the Achasan gate splits the sealing key

/theaters/0/prose.en:
At a provisional quarantine post below the Imjin embankment, a Sangha Relief State guide held the repatriation register to the flashlight's light.

The Seocho Computing Group escort wet its wheels on the mud road outside the gate, and the Sinnae transfer window opened the family waiting line first.

A jusa clerk of the Gwanghwamun Republic of Korea Government pointed at the ink bleed of a forged kinship certificate, and the Achasan gate post split its sealing key into two pieces.

Neither side condemned the northern regime; they kept only passage and registers.

/theaters/0/seoul_route/verified_geograp.en: Only the public terrain anchors — the Imjin–Han confluence and the northern transfer and refugee corridor — were used.

/theaters/0/seoul_route/outbound_boundar.en: The next waypoint beyond the Imjin embankment quarantine post and the actual manner of crossing the border were not set.

/theaters/0/seoul_route/fixed_duration.en: Not set. Movement cost and openness were judged by water level, quarantine waits, passage rights, and the state of the refugee columns.

/theaters/0/travel_constraints/rule.en: Closure was recorded not as deletion of the passage but as a state change carrying cause and reopening conditions.

/theaters/0/supply_chain/flows/0/handoff.en: The sealing ledger of goods was kept separate from the family register, and at every hand-off the seal state and receipt signature were left together.

/theaters/0/supply_chain/flows/1/handoff.en: Even when the escort ran late, custody of the capacitors and the quarantine judgment of persons were never gathered into one hand.

/theaters/0/supply_chain/flows/2/handoff.en: Reissue records never replaced the original; damage facts, issuer, and collation grounds were left on separate lines.

At the Han estuary provisional dock, the Water Compact sluice watch matched the tide table against the drainage valve.

The Standards Alliance director listened to the freezer compressor noise and changed the parts order, and the Yangjae Machineworks Company deputy set apart only the boxes whose seal hash was broken.

The Won Buddhist dharma officer did not erase the south-bank freezing order even when the power warning lamp lit.

The Yeouido Investment Union circulated only the dock safety bulletin, not price slogans.

/theaters/2/original_fiction.en: The Korea Strait Theater was a Seoul creative sea route in which Yongsan, City Hall, Myeongdong, Samsung, and Heukseok ran the three-leg relay docks and the interpretation windows. The canon-link table was detachable at any time.

Before the Line Succession State transshipment window, the signboards of the three relay legs blurred in the rain.

The Jeongdong General Labor Union branch chairman opened inland turn slots instead of the closed lane, and the Cathedral Accreditation State priest fixed the marriage and memorial accreditation seals.

The Sermon Registry State deacon handed over only sealed boxes and did not step into border talk.

The Heukseok interpretation window wrote foreign words beside Korean annotations, so the accord survived even with the private link table cleared away.

/theaters/3/original_fiction.en: The Duman River Far East Theater was a Seoul creative inland corridor in which Amsa, Sinnae, Gangnam, Jegi-dong, and Guui divided the rail detour and the mineral and fuel inspection.

/theaters/3/scenario_chains/1/summary.en: The Changdong wheel works divides the winter fuel queue and Jegi-dong receives the frostbitten

/theaters/3/scenario_chains/2/summary.en: The Achasan gate inspects the mineral-sample seals and scraps the forged origin tags

/theaters/3/prose.en:
In the Escort Protection State's freight yard, a car's weight sensor jumped too high for one car alone.

The Neutral Convoy City escort put that car into the detour slot, and the Seocho Computing Group deputy rewrote the winter fuel drum order.

The Medical Neutrality League sickbay dried the gloves of a frostbitten returning laborer, and the Gate Military Government company commander sealed the forged origin tag into an evidence envelope instead of the stove.

No one's government was condemned; only freight cars and people were inspected.

/theaters/4/prose.en:
On the roof of the Yeouido Investment Union hall, the residual-band lottery numbers went around.

The Water Compact sluice watch set the pump running times to those numbers, and a jusa clerk of the Republic of Korea Government posted the aid manifest hash in the citizen-observation cell.

The Jeongdong General Labor Union branch chairman opened a turn line carrying only the box of overseas remittance records, and the Yangjae Machineworks Company deputy switched off the orbital terminal's false-positive alarm.

The Myeongdong counseling window did not throw away the multilingual waiting tickets, however deep the night.

/theaters/4/supply_chain/flows/2/handoff.en: Counseling consent and remittance records were separated from the receipt and isolation judgment of aid goods.
