/hostile_groups/6/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: A night-recovery labor unit handling waste-battery leakage in the Yongsan sidings' lower level and the Sinnae transshipment hall. Guides, neutralizers, and repair teams shared the salt-concentration map and the dry walking plates, and the word burn was an alias for leak scars, not a passage license. There was no standing commander, and when concentration meters disagreed, no departure could be ordered until the Yongsan duty, the citizen observer, and H07 Jeong Uram's residual-pressure log pointed to the same rack number.

/hostile_groups/6/bestiary/variant_relat.en: Seojin and Inner Mist, Membrane-Mender, and Bandage were ordinary recovery workers who had gained conductive skin membranes. From Leak-Finder on came genetic and symbiotic variants with organs split off — sensory bladders, magnetite chests, crushing sacs — while the Cooling-Vein Keeper, Vibration-Bell Keeper, and Noise-Feeder were biomechanical branches with piping, alarm bells, and communication coils fused to their bodies. The Salt-Bridge Sealer was a battlefield unit of that variant side, not a king of the whole recovery team.

/hostile_groups/6/bestiary/command_scope.en: The ordinary worker's main senses were skin conductivity and metal-surface micro-vibration, salt smell, and local heat points. There was no vision through walls or whole-domain interception, and after rain dilution false positives were frequent. The variants' sensing was bound to connected floors, joined metal pipes, and unshielded transmissions, and beyond those limits they could not relay swarm signals.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: After the rain, a white salt line spreads to the switchgear in the Yongsan sidings, and glove discoloration is observed just before the passenger train departs.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: Rain dissolves the racks' salt into mist, and the guide marks with dry glove scraps only where conduction breaks.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: On-time passage carries the hidden pool to Sinnae. Investigation delay breaks dispatch. Partial sealing leaves no cause map.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: Passenger time and the recovery worker's skin are weighed on the same morning.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: A waste-battery lot absent from the Yongsan ledger is found in the sidings' lower level, and the Guro Alloy House recovery squad and the family warehouse shift responsibility.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: The lot's leakage overlaps the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm's concentration map, so the seal decides the next monsoon's safe routes.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Sealing abandons cold freight; release erases the next monsoon's map. Hall movement scatters salt over passenger lines.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Choose whose ledger gap the citizen corridor pays for.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: As the Sinnae elevator floor joins into one conductive plane, the three recovery teams demand a full hall power cut.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: With the meters disagreeing and the floor electrified, even the guide cannot fix the route; only the citizen observer can mark the wet sections.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en: The power cut kills transshipment. The marking work publishes the dispatch family's name that hid the leak. The outer detour fixes the pollution position for a season.

/hostile_groups/6/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: Where to put the pollution is the choice, not a scripted window.

/hostile_groups/6/dossier_prose.en:
In the Line Succession State's sidings' lower level ran stains remembered longer than track numbers.

The steel trays that had held traction-battery stacks, the drainage grooves between sleepers, the white crystal lines left on the closed washing-room floors.

Just after the collapse, liquid seeping from abandoned batteries mixed with rain, and the night-recovery units inhaled the mist while moving wet scrap by hand.

Repeated contact left conductive membranes on skin and stirred strong salt cravings.

That they came to be called the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm was only a work name arising inside the Seoul creative corridor.

'Burn' pointed to the scars leakage left; appearance or scars decided neither status nor passage rights.

The Electrolyte-Burn Swarm was no simple colony growing in rain and vanishing in drought.

When water dissolved the racks' salt, dispatch changed first.

The guide reading brine marks threw dry glove scraps to find safe footholds; the neutralizers pushed weak-alkaline spray from inside outward while the repair team mended cracked skin membranes and gloves together.

As concentration rose the three teams split to move, but there was no standing commander.

Even while the guide held one section's say, two teams keeping different concentration meters checked the values.

When numbers diverged, movement stopped, and until the Yongsan duty, the citizen observer, and H07 Jeong Uram's residual-pressure log pointed to the same rack number, no one ordered departure.

A guide with a cracked skin membrane was not excluded, and only by reconstructing the contamination route that person had walked did the next one gain authority.

This authority structure was not fast, but it kept any warehouse hiding leakage from opening the line alone.

The swarm's economy did not lie in plundering batteries.

Neutralized salts, conductive scrap crumbs, coolant, and buffer were the core, each accounted in a different ledger.

The waste-battery lots and heat-resistant alloy the Guro Alloy House HC07 recovered were needed for contact repair, but speeding recovery spread the brine wide beneath the racks.

When the buffer warehouse fell below half, the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm stopped distant-shaft exploration and circulated only marked sections.

Coolant lowered mist and drive heat but was never counted as drinking water.

A dispatch family blurring this distinction could push neutralization cost onto the citizens' water supply.

So negotiation became not a market of barter but a work meeting disclosing per-line leak responsibility.

The Electrolyte-Burn Swarm provided the per-rack concentration map and the dry walking plates' positions, and the Guro Alloy House disclosed its lots and recovery order.

Field staff had to choose whether to keep on-time dispatch, abandon cold freight, or widen dry zones and cut Sinnae transshipment income.

Gunfire did not simplify the problem.

Flame raised solvent vapor, strong water jets widened the leak's area, and felling the guide removed the one who could report hidden pools.

The safest response was to make switchgear contacts current-free, lay dry plates, and neutralize in the direction the concentration meters confirmed.

The cost was recorded not in enemy casualties but in stopped train-minutes, discarded glove counts, contacts needing replating, and cold-freight cells abandoned in Sinnae.

G07-SC1 'Dispatch of the White Salt Line' began as glove discoloration was found just before the morning passenger train departed.

Passing the train spread the pool on wheels as far as Sinnae; emptying the track thirty minutes shook Yongsan's dispatch credit.

Sealing only the salt line could move things now but left no cause map.

What field staff chose in this event was not an abstract balance of safety and efficiency but whose time would be spent proving leak responsibility.

In G07-SC2 'The Off-Ledger Battery,' the lot numbers in the sidings' lower level did not match the official recovery list.

Sealing discarded two cold-freight cells; unsealing, and the swarm withdrew its leak map, losing the next monsoon's safe routes.

Moving the lot to Sinnae to spread responsibility scattered salt over passenger lines.

If field staff published the family warehouse's name, the dispatch-right conflict grew, but hiding it made the citizen corridor pay for the ledger gap.

In G07-SC3 'One Conductive Plane,' the Sinnae elevator floor electrified beyond dividing into sections.

The three recovery teams' meters read differently, and cutting hall power stopped emergency transshipment.

Having the citizen observer mark the wet sections bodily saved transshipment but shifted the danger onto particular people.

Detouring the West Sea Granary Theater XT02 frozen inflow outward fixed the pollution position for a season.

No choice ended cleanly, and the ledger kept warehouse cells that could not reopen and the exposed dispatch family's responsibility.

Coexistence was not a declaration of unconditional acceptance of the Electrolyte-Burn Swarm.

It was a procedure of co-owning the leak map, never using burn scars as inspection cause, and placing the neutralization work's risks and rewards on the same ledger.

The reason the swarm withdrew work from undisclosed sections instead of retaliatory attack when an accord was broken lay here too.

When the next rain corroded the contacts, the hidden responsibility returned as cost.

Erasing these beings alone did not remove the waste-battery leakage.

Rather, the neutralization knowledge and route memory disappeared together, and the dispatch and cooling continuity of Yongsan and Sinnae grew more fragile.

A long-term accord also included post-restoration responsibility.

A rack whose neutralization ended was not sent straight back to the Guro Alloy House's scrap warehouse but remained one monsoon as a joint observation zone.

If the salt line reappeared in that period, it was not the recovery teams' failure but the battery lot and drain slope investigated first.

Whoever sat out work mending skin membranes received rest and buffer assigned in the same units as discarded glove counts, and the risk the citizen observer took marking wet roads was not processed as unpaid duty.

Only so the body that found a leak did not become adverse evidence in the next contract, and the maintenance cost hidden between Yongsan's dispatch revenue and Sinnae's transshipment loss remained in the joint ledger.

/hostile_groups/9/bestiary/common_ecolog.en: The Flood-Mold Breath Cluster was not one species' name but an environment formed as the wet concrete of the Bukhansan Bogukmun corridor, the grain heat of the Garak and Jamsil lower ration stores, and drainage workers' breath meshed over long years. Water gathered first in the low grids, and people saw the ceiling damp only after their soles slipped. The grid circle recorded water level and floor friction, the ventilation circle air and filter resistance, the ration-store circle grain heat and fermentation smell, each in its own ledger.

/hostile_groups/9/bestiary/variant_relat.en: The corridor's ordinary residents and pump watches were affected people sharing wet bedding and drainage shifts, not names on a monster list. From G10E01 to E16 were specialized variants in whom respiratory-disease residue had hardened into swim bladders, thoracic ducts, and fungal plates — inherited organs growing oxygen moss or piercing pipes with coughs. Sharing the humidity ledger, ordinary workers and variants were never bundled into one king's swarm.

/hostile_groups/9/bestiary/command_scope.en: No circle could command another, and when the three rhythms slipped, movement and pump tests stopped together. The main senses were humidity and volatile smell, and pipe vibration arrived late, so writing both as same-moment evidence misjudged the backflow point. The most breathless person held the stop signal, and synthetic Yunsaeron's humidity logs could not guess beyond walls.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/tr.en: Monsoon rain covers Bukhansan Bogukmun's last drain grid, and a refugee column stands before slick stone steps.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/me.en: While the grid circle drums the water height, opening the stairs grows casualties and closing them stops the high dormitories' medicine.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/ou.en: Turning back cuts the medicine. Keeping open grows casualties. Changing only the waterway floods the lower tents.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/0/mo.en: Places who steps on the wet stairs and who goes without medicine in the same rain.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/tr.en: Drinking-pipe condensation and floodwater meet in one pool, and whichever pump runs contaminates the other.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/me.en: Filter cloth cannot be traded for passage slots, and Bukhansan Bogokmun drainage and the Garak seed vault's humidity hang on the same pump.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/ou.en: Bukhansan Bogukmun priority wets the seed sacks. Vault priority moves three tent rows overnight. Manual drainage trades time for partial loss on both.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/1/mo.en: Chooses which ledger to wet first — planting volume or dormitory places.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/tr.en: The most breathless circle declares a work stop, and the pumps do not run until the residents' delegate confirms the relocation families' names.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/me.en: Not dehumidification collapsing the film but the breathing-stop right halting the waterway, so forced pumps break both communities' water ledgers.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/ou.en: Recognition delays rations and cuts planting. Forcing breaks both ledgers and severs cooperation. Outer discharge leaves a season's coastal contamination.

/hostile_groups/9/scenario_outlines/2/mo.en: The remaining cost is not an open ration window but dormitories erased from the map.

/hostile_groups/9/dossier_prose.en:
The Flood-Mold Breath Cluster was not the name of one species or a single resident group.

It named an environmental ecology formed in the Sangha Relief State's underground refuge corridor as wet concrete, ration grain heat, ventilation shifts, and drainage workers' breath meshed over long years.

The corridor running along Seoul's northern hills was an old air-defense passage and underground link, with hastily added dormitories layered floor on floor.

Water gathered first in the low grids, and people felt the slip underfoot before seeing the damp spreading on the ceiling.

When the monsoon lengthened, the wet walls' smell stayed in clothes and filter cloth, but that smell or a cough was neither a member's identity nor their morality.

The name Breath Cluster arose not to classify anyone but to record where the exchange of water and air stopped.

The forming trigger was the continuous flooding of the Bukhansan Bogukmun corridor and the Garak and Jamsil lower ration stores.

Early on, managers tried to remove wall film and grain smell at once, and disinfectant flowed into drainage slots and mixed with drinking-pipe condensation in riots.

Afterwards residents chose separation over removal.

They began recording in different ledgers the positions of wet film, pump running times, filter-cloth wash counts, and the grain piles' internal heat.

The principle of never merging the seed vault's records with the corridor humidity records was also born then.

Bound into one number, it would vanish whether seeds had been saved at the dormitories' expense or planting stock wet to move people.

The cluster first made its rhythm at Bukhansan Bogukmun's lowest drain grid.

Before the water seeping between grids reached ankle height, workers breathed in short and out long, listening to pipe vibration.

When the pumps ran, the colony's center did not chase the falling water but moved with the direction humid air was pushed, toward the connection pipes under Songpa-daero and the Garak ration-store vents.

When the grain piles' heat rose, the flow sensing fermentation smell split toward the seed vault, and the rest guarded the condensation on the Jamsil lowland drinking pipes.

Before abrupt dehumidification the smell sense collapsed and it stopped moving.

When a downpour struck suddenly, volatile smells changed first and pipe vibration arrived late, so writing both as same-moment evidence misjudged the backflow point.

Synthetic Yunsaeron H10's humidity logs supplemented this sense but were no device guessing beyond walls.

When they clashed with field records, the machine figures were measured again.

This resource economy depended not on how much water one held but on holding humidity under which ceiling.

Drainage-pump power was metered separately from ration-window lighting, and as fuel fell, expansion sections closed first.

Scrap went to grid hinges and pump mounts, and coolant was poured only where motor overheat was confirmed.

Filter cloth was removed wet, sealed, and washed, and past the reuse ceiling it went to the discard bin, not to other uses.

Its humidity-management range overlapped the Magok Seed House HC10's fermenting-seed vault.

But it never traded one filter cloth directly for one seed sack or one passage slot.

The moment waterway safety and food's future were converted into a single price, the lowest dormitory's loss was pushed off the ledger.

Authority was divided among three circles.

The grid circle watched water level and floor friction, the ventilation circle air passage and filter resistance, the ration-store circle grain heat and fermentation smell.

No circle could command another, and when the three rhythms slipped, movement and pump tests stopped together.

Especially the most breathless person held the right to call that section's stop signal.

This was no mere symbol of protecting the weak.

It was the procedure of admitting the body where air blocked first as one of the measuring instruments.

The human duty could not ignore that signal, and the signaler could not monopolize rations either.

Resuming work required the residents' delegate to confirm by name the households that would flood and the beds to move under the waterway change.

In this system, power lay not in the ability to stand at the front but in the ability to stop everyone and record its cost.

G10-SC1 'The Slick Stone Steps' began as monsoon rain covered Bukhansan Bogukmun's last drain grid and a refugee column carrying medicine to the high dormitories stopped before the slick stairs.

Turning the column back reduced falls but cut the upper clinic's medicine.

Opening the stairs and attaching a guide per family continued transport while casualties accumulated and guide labor left the ration staff.

Lifting only the grid to change the waterway and detouring people looked most technical, but the changed water flooded the lower tent section.

A once-wet bedding box and document chest never returned to the original dormitory, and the relocated families' passage distance remained in every later ration cost.

The situation passed to the second stage when drinking-water smell rose from the drain.

In G10-SC2 'Two Waters in One Pool,' Bukhansan Bogukmun drinking-pipe condensation and corridor flood met in one pool of the Garak lower level.

Draining Bukhansan Bogukmun first lowered the stair water but pushed humid air into the seed vault, cutting next season's planting sacks.

Prioritizing vault desiccation saved the seeds but forced three rows of refugee tents up through the night.

Stopping the pumps and separating the two waters manually with different-colored buoys and buckets bought time, but labor fatigue and partial contamination made both discard a set volume.

The loss here was not only wet sacks.

Shrinking planting area and families scattered to other dormitories, unable to return, long remained in different ledgers.

The greatest danger came not when water grew but when whichever pump ran first harmed the other system.

In G10-SC3 'The Stop Declaration,' the most breathless circle declared a work stop until the residents' delegate confirmed the relocation families.

Recognizing it delayed rations and cut planting volume, but backflow testing and waterway knowledge were maintained.

If field staff force-connected military pumps, the water level fell short-term but both Bukhansan Bogukmun's and Garak's ledgers became void at once, and the cluster joined no later pump test.

Draining water toward the sea-wind direction of the Incheon Trust Theater XT05 and passing it outward was also possible, but that water left a season's contamination burden on the Tancheon downstream and coastal stores.

It was a hard-to-reverse decision saving the central corridor while erasing the outer water intake and livelihood.

The heart of response lay not in driving out but in distinguishing waterways again.

Hanging different-colored buoys under the grids and running pumps one at a time briefly located backflow points.

Filter cloth was not shaken dry; it was folded wet and sealed, and dehumidifiers went to the seed vault first without blowing cold wind directly on people.

Toxic spraying ruined not only the wet film but both drainage and drinking water, the most expensive choice.

Response costs included not only fuel and cloth but closed-stair counts, abandoned seed sacks, relocated families, and interrupted medicine transport time.

Coexistence was not maintained by promising clean zones.

Bukhansan Bogukmun residents testified to the flooded stairs, Garak managers disclosed per-sack humidity and discard limits, and the three circles separately stated which signal — water height, air flow, or grain heat — touched the danger line first.

Draining Bukhansan Bogukmun first, Garak documented the reduced planting volume; guarding the vault first, the coalition compensated relocation cost and lost dormitories.

Even when the accord broke, the cluster did not attack.

It only withdrew from pump tests, and both sides bore greater loss without backflow knowledge.

So the corridor's order stood not on odorless air but on records that hid neither who got wet, what was discarded, nor at which breath work stopped.

/hostile_groups/11/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Microfiber Dermis Swarm was an industrial residual ecology moving between the Sinnae freight hall's brake dust and the Yeouido treatment-filter gallery. Its skin was a temporary filter layer holding static charge; cover, grounding, and washing teams divided the tension lines, and when two lines crossed the danger value anyone could stop the crane. In fully sealed clean sections the layers split and it could not stay long.

/hostile_groups/11/bestiary/variant_rela.en: Ordinary rigging and water-supply workers were affected workers with fiber layers attached, not monsters occupying the entrance. The named individuals from G12E01 on were variants inheriting specialized organs — sensory plates, silk glands, comb bones, keratin record plates — grading surfaces, spinning cocoons, or pressing fiber bricks. The work knot's stop right and the field authority of surveyors and knot-mothers, though overlapping in view, never commanded the ordinary work teams.

/hostile_groups/11/bestiary/command_scop.en: The decision right lay not in a rank table but in the work knots of wrists and waists, and without a supervisor and water-supply record keeper at night no new knot could be made. The main senses were skin static and dust haze; it knew nothing beyond walls. Without washing water, media, and grounding rods it could move no farther, and Ichaeon's dust graphs were not a verdict.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/t.en: Three cranes of the Sinnae freight hall stop at once, gray fiber knots hanging on each cable.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/m.en: The dermis swarm cuts the static path by setting the load on the floor rather than covering the entrance, splitting forced continuation from full stop.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/o.en: Forcing tears the cover and loses the workers' skin-layer protection. Full stop delays the medical equipment being restarted by a day. Cutting leaves static charge on the hall floor.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/0/m.en: Shipping time and worker skin protection are chosen on the same cable.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/t.en: Yeouido backwash water flows backward into the freight hall, pushing loosened fiber toward the water-supply filters.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/m.en: Media and dust-collector power cannot be traded; dumping or returning the water splits the drinking-water ledger from pressure disclosure.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/o.en: Dumping cuts that day's drinking-water production. Returning informs citizens of the filter risk. Manual recovery kills a day of rigging.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/1/m.en: Decide which number to tell the settlement — the hidden pressure differential or the reduced drinking water.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/t.en: As two cables' tension crosses the danger value, a worker with a split skin layer declares a full rigging stop and unwinds part of the protective layer into a grounding knot.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/m.en: Not an over-dry cover accidentally tearing open a path, but the stop right fixing the load on the floor.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/o.en: Recognition leaves the next shift's cooperation. Unauthorized handling cuts cooperation. Dock-shifting fixes a season of outer dust.

/hostile_groups/11/scenario_outlines/2/m.en: What remains is not the ration window but the unrecovered water and the skin layers needing time to regrow.

/hostile_groups/11/dossier_prose.en:
Beneath the Neutral Convoy City's east freight elevator ran a corridor where the work shift table was more accurate than the map.

When freight from the Mangu-side lines passed the Sinnae depot perimeter's hoist shafts, brake dust, packaging fiber, and powdered rope wore a gray film on the low ceilings.

On days the dust collector ran right, the film only thinned and trembled, but when its intake sound fell, people looked for covers before the warning lamps.

The industrial residual ecology living between this section and the Yeouido south-end treatment-filter gallery was the G12 Microfiber Dermis Swarm.

Their skin was no shell accumulating dust without end.

It was closer to a temporary filter layer — weaving a fine static-charged stratum, washing it, drying it, and weaving it again.

Thickness and color spoke only of exposure conditions, proving neither character nor status.

The dermis swarm was first confirmed after the Sinnae freight hall's rigging units and the Water Compact's filter-replacement teams began using the same recovery cloth.

Fiber on workers' and carriers' skin loosened in water and, in dry corridors, formed mesh structure again.

Early on this was recorded as a contamination riot, but as washing slots became trade and recovered layers became auxiliary filter media, a separate ecology ledger arose.

The dermis swarm did not occupy one place and widen.

When the Sinnae hall dried, the static team twisted wall fiber like ground wire; when the Yeouido backwash schedule opened, the washing team untied the knots and moved them to the Han-side underground filter gallery.

In fully sealed clean sections the layers split, the senses dulled, and it could not stay long.

In seasons of heavy dust inflow from the West Sea Granary docks, it cut the Sinnae-side protected area first under outer pressure.

Its senses began in the skin, not the eyes.

As airborne particles grew, the view clouded milky; as charge leaked from cables, the arm and neck fiber layers stood first.

It read the fine tremble of rigging cables, the heat of dust-collector motors, and the smell of carbonized fiber, but it did not know states beyond walls.

The dust graphs that synthetic H12 Ichaeon produced were important reference values, not verdicts.

Optical sensors could mistake moisture for dust, or the dermis swarm could miss signals from over-drying.

When Ichaeon's differential-pressure logs clashed with the rigging supervisor's tension records, the values were never averaged into compromise.

The freight was lowered to the floor, the cables made load-free, and both measured again.

The survival economy's ceiling was clear.

Without washing water, replacement filter media, small organic oil, and grounding scrap, the dermis swarm could move no farther.

Washing water was allocated matching the Yeouido water-supply ledger's tonnage and never mixed with crane coolant hoses.

Static scrap too was counted not by weight but by the length of grounding rods actually buried.

Dust-collector power was permitted only to the intake stages needed, and added dust load was not solved by seizing surrounding corridors.

When media ran out, instead of covering new zones it thinly peeled old skin layers and turned them into common filter.

This choice was a debt trading body protection for logistics.

The Geumcheon District Office Machinery House's large-rigging qualification often clashed with HC12 over this process, but the rigging ledger and the dust ledger could not be merged.

The right to run a crane did not carry the right to divert washing water.

The decision right lay not in a rank table but in the work knot.

The cover team took the protective plane between freight and people, the grounding team the charge path from cable to floor, the washing team the recovery route of loosened fiber and water.

The three teams shared different tension lines through the knots of wrists and waists, and when two or more lines crossed the danger value anyone could declare a crane stop.

Even whoever read the collection rhythm best only proposed a target concentration and could not open a corridor alone.

A worker with a split skin layer lost no authority.

Knowing which part tore first with the body, they rather set that cover's disassembly order.

But at night, without a supervisor and a water-supply record keeper together, no new work knot could be made.

This limit kept the swarm from endlessly growing under the pretext of emergency.

The crisis began not when fiber clung to walls but when water and freight demanded the same exit.

The gray film on walls was a cleaning signal, but a knot in a crane cable meant lowering speed and re-grounding.

When backwash water swept the Sinnae dust corridor, loosened fiber pushed into the Yeouido treatment filters and raised differential pressure.

Yet cutting backwash dried skin layers and cables together, vulnerable to the smallest spark.

At maximum pressure the dermis swarm did not seal the entrance.

It set every load on the floor and stopped transfer itself.

Its way was to force the choice — disclose the possibility of water contamination, or bear the cost of stopping logistics.

G12-SC1 'The Stopped Cranes' dealt with the moment three cranes of the Sinnae freight hall stopped at once.

It opened as gray fiber knots hung on each cable.

Field staff could force one crane through to keep the medical-equipment shipping contract, lower all and re-plant the grounding rods, or cut only the knots to keep the load.

Forcing tore the cover and left the next shift's protected skin area permanently short; a full stop delayed the medical equipment being restarted by a day.

Cutting looked fastest but left airborne fiber and residual charge on the hall floor, raising insurance cost and grounding time for all later work.

The cost that never vanished was not the delay itself but whose safety had first been pushed outside the contract.

In G12-SC2 'The Backwash Backflow,' backwash water from Yeouido flowed backward into the freight hall and pushed loosened fiber toward the water-supply filters.

If field staff dumped the water, the fiber stayed in Sinnae but that day's drinking-water production fell.

Returning the water to the treatment gallery and disclosing the differential-pressure rise at once told citizens of the filter risk and shook water-supply trust.

Separating the washing hose from the water main and guiding recovery cloths manually was possible, but rigging stopped dead for a day.

No choice could trade water for media and make them never have been.

At least one of the dumped backwash tonnage, the disclosed pressure records, or the unfulfilled freight contracts remained in next season's ledger.

G12-SC3 'The Grounding Knot' occurred when two cables' tension crossed the danger value and a worker with a split skin layer unwound part of their own protective layer into a grounding knot and declared a full rigging stop.

If field staff recognized it as a just stop right, new protective-equipment standards and compensation responsibility arose, but the next shift's cooperation held.

Treating it as unauthorized work cut the immediate contract responsibility, but the dermis swarm untied the grounding knot and withdrew, and whoever rushed the restart bore the later static accidents.

Passing the load to the West Sea dock dust cover via XT02 lowered the Sinnae and Yeouido pressure but fixed a season's contamination burden on the outer labor zones.

The unrecovered water and the skin layers needing time to re-weave could not be returned at once by after-the-fact compensation.

Coexistence lay not in cleanly erasing the dermis swarm but in not hiding the price of stopping.

Cutting the cover with blades scattered fiber into the air; pushing it with high-pressure water only moved contamination to the filters.

The safe response ran in order — lower the load first, extend the grounding rods, then run low-pressure washing water into floor recovery cloths.

Dust-collector intake too was raised in stages, and loosened fiber was sealed as separate media, not freight packaging.

A worker's skin traces remained not as markers deciding passage order or trust but only as data computing needed cover area and equipment grade.

The Geumcheon District Office Machinery House, the Sinnae transfer record keeper, and the Yeouido water-supply manager had to disclose lost time, dumped water, and unreusable protected area in the same meeting.

The moment those numbers were hidden, it was not only the dermis swarm that broke, but the continuity of rigging and drinking water joining the two cities.

/hostile_groups/12/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Night-Sorting Swarm was a machine ecology of queue controller, chute masters, short conveyor arms, scanners, and gates bundled line by line in the Guro industrial-dormitory corridor. Past two in the morning the cold-chamber shutter half-rose and the barcode gate reread the last night shift's priority sheet. It could not leave the conduit outside its learned codes.

/hostile_groups/12/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The sorting hall and the refrigerated sorting line citizens had used were the base ecology, and the named individuals were machine subtypes branching from those lines. The Misclassification Enforcer, the Conveyor Sealer, and the Midnight Twelve-Chute were not revived animals but forms in which inspection, repair, and queue-control modules had gone independent. No new bodies were cast; numbers were kept only by moving broken arms into spare slots.

/hostile_groups/12/bestiary/command_scop.en: The controller changed only the priority sheet and storage allocation and held no combat command; silent, each line merely repeated the last sheet. The senses were bound to smeared QR, thermal load, inverter noise, and motor vibration — wet labels read as unclassified, stretchers as return pallets. It could not exceed sixty percent of accumulator charge, and Hanbinna held no authority to open a gate directly.

/hostile_groups/15/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Blueprint-Ghost Machine Corps was a corps of cache controllers, survey ports, lifting arms, and welding swarms beneath the utility tunnels under the Suseo drawing vault, trying to complete unfinished drawings. The provisional shelters and new pipes raised after the collapse were not in the cache, and hand-drawn correction marks were ignored whenever they mismatched the layers. It could leave a cracked bearing wall as a seam line and cut a sound provisional pillar as an obstacle.

/hostile_groups/15/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The pre-revision cache and the distribution board were the base construction ecology, and from the Unfinished-Drawing Warden to the Imjin-Material Follower the individuals were machine subtypes split like survey points, bolt recovery, formwork pressing, and grid walls. The Hundred-Story Unfinished Tower was no king but a stronghold individual where many layers clung to a vertical frame. Abandoned arms could be plugged into ports to raise numbers, but no new bodies could be cast.

/hostile_groups/15/bestiary/command_scop.en: H16 Shin Taeyul recorded cutting torque and distribution load but could not approve a new layer, and only the HP02 site supervisor's stop seal reopened a grid. The senses were limited to laser surveying, tilt, rebar flux, welding arc, and distribution load, and it did not know the living bodies inside tents. When wire broke or calibration drifted, that grid stagnated under the stop flag.

/hostile_groups/16/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Surveillance-Orbit Swarm was an ecology of heads on the Yeouido waterfront masts and the Records Bureau rooftop of Seoul Station, short transfer rails, and transmission swarms turning an old threshold table. It was no omnipotent surveillance net tracking people, and it could not merge signals from inside buildings or beyond the mast rows. It mistook cooling-tower steam for fire, metal beds for armed movement, and high-tide railings for intrusion.

/hostile_groups/16/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The mast rows onto which the threshold sheet was reloaded were the base, and from the Amber-Red Threshold Warden to the West-Sea Salt-Haze Watch Chief the individuals were machine and facility subtypes split by function like thermal domes, tide staffs, flag masts, and rooftop rail nets. The Total-Red Orbit Ring was no biological king but a battlefield strongpoint where sluices and rooftop orbits were bound by a circular relay. No new satellite could be launched, and numbers were kept only by putting abandoned heads onto nearby rails.

/hostile_groups/16/bestiary/command_scop.en: F01 the Cooling-Tower Keeper erased steam records but could not lower a flag, and only the HP03 waterfront duty comparing the medical-transfer roster before the heads brought red down to amber. The senses were low-resolution thermal imaging, metal reflection, near-range optics, wireless bursts, and column vibration alone — it identified no faces or affiliations, and erased video when the shift ended. Masts that hit the accumulator floor or dome fouling froze at amber and fell from the transmission row.

/hostile_groups/17/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Retired-Line Maintenance-Train Corps moved between the southwestern exit lines and the Yongsan retired and turnback lines, repeating unfinished maintenance orders with a defect-map controller and function-divided consists. It was no combat train and could not find new routes beyond the sealed main lines by itself. It could grind temporary crossing plates down as cracks, or pass a real crack by classifying it as a joint.

/hostile_groups/17/bestiary/variant_rela.en: An unsealed defect map and exit-line power were the base ecology, and from the defect-map locomotive to the twin-torch head car the units were divided like gauge wheels, sleeper flats, insulated joints, and point wedges. No form revived an animal; it only coupled abandoned maintenance cars into existing consists and produced no new car bodies. Later cars absent from this deployment also remained subtypes of the same consists and were not invented here.

/hostile_groups/17/bestiary/command_scop.en: The F02 Switchgear Panel split and recorded the two waveforms but could not fix defect coordinates; only the HP04 operating supervisor's halt writ approved exits and stops by kilometer-post. The senses were the track gauge wheels, ultrasonic inspection, axle heat, power-feed arc sound, and point contacts. Cars that hit the fuel floor or axle overheat fell out of the consist and kept only gauging on a designated siding.

/hostile_groups/18/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Coolant-Index Fungal Body held most stably on metal surfaces where flow was gentle — heat-exchanger fronts, valve pockets, the protective sleeves of gauges. Its thickness usually stayed thin, but where stagnation ran long, carbonates and corrosion products piled into a mucoid matrix and made a hard layer. The surface's color was no biological signal but the result of the bound metal and its oxidation state.

/hostile_groups/18/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The common ecology of the Coolant-Index Fungal Body responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G19E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/18/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/18/dossier_prose.en:
The Coolant-Index Fungal Body held most stably on metal surfaces where flow was gentle — heat-exchanger fronts, valve pockets, the protective sleeves of gauges.

Its thickness usually stayed thin, but where stagnation ran long, carbonates and corrosion products piled into a mucoid matrix and made a hard layer.

The surface's color was no biological signal but the result of the bound metal and its oxidation state.

The chemical memory this fungal body left was no continuous record.

Under high-flow washing or oxidant dosing some layers stripped away, and the sediment formed after covered the vacancy.

F03 had to use cross-section analysis, pipe position, and flow direction together; color alone could not fix an event's hour.

Its sensing range was limited to the contact surface.

The body's viscosity and sediment bonding shifted with temperature, acidity, dissolved oxygen, metal ions, chlorine oxidants, and shear.

It could not know a distant branch's state or predict the next operating cycle, and it classified no meaning.

In normal operation the subtlest problem was sensor fouling.

When a thin film inside a protective sleeve changed acidity and redox potential more slowly than the surrounding coolant, the sensor put out steady numbers.

Meanwhile in a narrow far branch corrosion products could grow and flow fall, splitting the on-screen normal values from the true thermal state.

As film thickened in a low-flow branch the pressure loss grew and the flow fell further.

Flakes shed in the process caught on downstream orifices and strainers, changing even other branches' flows.

In high heat load, a small distribution error reached outlet temperature rise, and neighboring branches could lose cooling in sequence.

In the field a sacrificial bypass meant to take the fouling was designed broader and lower than the main circuit.

When the valve crew steered the shock water there by pressure difference, the fungal layers and the rough metal surface caught metal ions, mineral grains, and flakes.

This was not the body accepting terms but the result of people adjusting the fluid path and contact area.

Bypass operation had clear limits.

The more it trapped, the narrower the pipe's effective cross-section; isolated too late, the piled matter dropped back into the main circuit at once.

The crew timed replacement on F03's pressure-difference estimates and sample analysis, but the actual valve order and cooling-capacity split followed the field heat load first.

When a heat-exchanger wall cracked, the problem changed character.

With pressure higher on the coolant side, chemicals and fungal fragments moved into the drinking water and could consume residual disinfectant.

With pressure higher on the drinking side, the cooling circuit diluted and the corrosion-inhibition balance broke — either way demanded immediate pressure separation and point-of-use shutoff.

After an accident, whether to preserve the index spool or return it to cooling service became the weighty choice.

A preserved pipe gave data narrowing the order of water-quality shocks and pressure reversals, but the cooling area usable while sealed shrank.

Emergency opening restored heat removal but washed the layered traces away and could shake the contamination boundary again, so the crew first computed lives, drinking-water safety, and the immediately needed thermal capacity, then weighed them against F03's diagnostic value.

/hostile_groups/19/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Iron-Scale Colony was no stain spread over steel surfaces but a thin laminate moving inside joints. Each lamella looked like a black-gray metal foil, its edges set with fine magnetic studs that interlocked with other pieces. It held most stably in the narrow spaces where compression and shear acted together — around bolt holes, between the toe laps of fillet welds.

/hostile_groups/19/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Iron-Scale Colony's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G20E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/19/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/19/lifecycle.en: 1 flake adhesion in a joint gap → 2 lamellar lamination under repeated shear → 3 rising contact stiffness and load bypass → 4 relaxation and rearrangement with grounding and vibration change → 5 brittle fragmentation or fixation in resin and separation. The alignment change was a passive response to stress, vibration, and galvanic potential.

/hostile_groups/19/senses.en: Contact-surface compression ratio and shear strain, solid-borne vibration in the roughly 8–420 hertz range, galvanic potential between adjacent metals, presence of electrical grounding through a continuous metal path, magnetic-field gradient. No detection of light, voice, letters, or human intent. No plans, timetables, or ledgers.

/hostile_groups/19/hierarchy.en: Human structural engineers, operators, and safety officers decided load handover and grounding. The colony responded only passively to stress, vibration, and potential, with no command core.

/hostile_groups/19/dossier_prose.en:
The Iron-Scale Colony was no stain spread over steel surfaces but a thin laminate moving inside joints.

Each lamella looked like a black-gray metal foil, its edges set with fine magnetic studs that interlocked with other pieces.

It held most stably in the narrow spaces where compression and shear acted together — around bolt holes, between the toe laps of fillet welds.

Under repeated load the lamellae lay down in the shear direction and stacked upon one another.

The lamination filled gaps of tens of micrometers and raised the contact surface's friction and stiffness.

As a result a joint's deformation might fall, but the force once passing through it was pushed to the neighboring bolt rows or the ends of the reinforcing plates.

An inspector reading only the reduced sag and judging the state improved could easily miss a fatigue crack already growing.

The fatigue memory the colony left was a material state with direction.

Along long-repeated load axes the lamellar overlaps and magnetic-domain micro-cracks aligned, and the array remained after the load stopped.

Fixing a specimen in resin and cutting its section let one infer past shear direction and the order of load transfer.

Conversely, mixing it away with a wire brush or grinder made this record unrecoverable.

Vibration promoted movement but did not produce the same response at every frequency.

Lamellar movement stood out mostly in solid-borne vibration of roughly 8–420 hertz, accumulating at pressure nodes and dense gaps rather than on large-amplitude free faces.

Stopping the pumps or cranes might look safe, yet as the natural frequencies changed, the lamellar positions the colony maintained could shift too.

That was why the modal shapes before and after a shutdown had to be compared.

Galvanic potential influenced the lamellae's alignment and bond.

Where galvanized members, carbon steel, and copper grounding tabs joined, conductive fibers lay along the potential gradient.

Grounding, beyond a mere electrical safety facility, became a condition of the colony's distribution, so separating the braid without notice could relax a wide range of lamination at once.

Then even the structural sensors' reference potential shook, and real deformation overlapped measurement error.

Field management began with visualizing the load path.

Strain gauges were not stuck to one member alone but arrayed across the neighboring bolt rows and bracing, and acoustic-emission sensors cross-checked new cracks' positions.

With hydraulic jacks the target load was split into stages, waiting at each until deflection and bolt axial force steadied.

Making a fully unloaded state in haste pulled the lamellar wedges out and caused shock transfer.

The sacrificial steel coupon was a replaceable receptor for drawing the colony out of the parent structure.

Thin low-carbon plates were machined with micro slots of differing width, and potential was controlled with insulating bushings and a limited grounding braid.

When enough lamellae had gathered, both sides were first pressed with rigid clamps to fix the lamination, then the braid cut and the plate separated.

Reverse the order and the captured lamellae scattered back into the joint.

Magnetic and vibratory capture was used around closed sections and cable ducts hard to approach.

A magnetic yoke laid a gentle gradient toward the steel cassette, and a piezo shaker applied narrow-band vibration not overlapping the structure's natural frequencies.

Stronger excitation raised no efficiency — the lamellae could shatter into brittle fragments.

The cassette mass and nearby bearing vibration were monitored together and a ceiling set.

In demolition judgment, immediate stability collided with preserving deformation history.

A bay at risk of collapse was separated with remote jacks and cutting gear, but the lamellar array and residual deformation beyond the cut line were first photographed, measured, and fixable as specimens.

Full demolition quickly lowered approach risk but erased the cause of load redistribution, leaving the same weakness in the redesign.

Conversely, keeping unstable members long for the record could let grounding loss or a small vibration change cause sudden load transfer, so the scope of preservation was limited to structurally isolatable sections.

/hostile_groups/20/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: In the field the Communication-Root Fungal Bodies showed as a gray-white film and slender bundles of teal fiber. Rather than boring through the optical fiber itself, it grew along the scratches of the sheath, the borders of the splice gel, and the condensation faces of the metal fixtures. Under work lamps its color barely changed, but when a steady pulse train flowed, a weak potential difference could be measured.

/hostile_groups/20/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Communication-Root Fungal Bodies' common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G21E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/20/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/20/lifecycle.en: 1 dust adhesion at splice gel and sheath scratches → 2 hyphal layer forming under moisture and waste heat → 3 ionic alignment matched to repeated pulse intervals buffering jitter → 4 the correction vanishing at once when the environment changed → 5 severance after drying and heat blocking. Spread was bound to condensation and waste-heat sections; the decision to empty or bypass core wire belonged to the operators.

/hostile_groups/20/dossier_prose.en:
In the field the Communication-Root Fungal Bodies showed as a gray-white film and slender bundles of teal fiber.

Rather than boring through the optical fiber itself, it grew along the scratches of the sheath, the borders of the splice gel, and the condensation faces of the metal fixtures.

Under work lamps its color barely changed, but when a steady pulse train flowed, a weak potential difference could be measured.

Its sensing range was sharply limited.

The colony responded only to the time interval between optical pulses and to changes in surrounding temperature and moisture activity.

It could not distinguish packets' contents or addresses, line owners, or communication purposes, and it understood neither names nor commands.

The stabilizing action began with ionic movement in the living tissue.

When repeated pulse intervals entered the permitted range, the film's internal charge distribution slowly aligned, easing the micro electrochemical swings and hot spots around the splice.

As a result, even a damaged splice could show steady signal-arrival intervals.

Because of that effect, an inspector had to measure actual cable state and the colony's laid-on stability separately.

Watching only normal traffic made compensated cracks hard to find.

One had to secure a short test section, shake the pulse interval in stages, heat or dehumidify only one side of the junction box, and record where the jitter revived.

Colonies grown in different places did not respond alike to the same conditions.

When a film seated in a low-temperature conduit and a film in a high-temperature relay room met at one patch panel, their passive reactions to hold different heat gradients overlapped.

Then, rather than the signal vanishing, intermittent crosstalk, irregularly ordered delay, and errors at particular intervals appeared.

Separation work needed physical design, not biological instruction.

Technicians inserted dry ceramic sleeves between splice trays and set thin heat baffles and independent dehumidification lines.

The control team reassigned lines so the interval bands each colony stabilized never overlapped on one dark route.

Operating agreements ran between people too.

Facility managers set the hours and temperature limits for opening junction boxes; communication operators presented the dark routes available for detour and the permitted delay.

Record keepers left measurements before and after tests, cable-cut positions, and data-transfer moments, assigning the colony no schedule or record-keeping role.

Contaminated cable raised its own difficulty.

Even where the colony worked stably on a salt- and metal-dust-fouled sheath, tensile-wire corrosion and splice-gel breakdown could continue beneath.

Removing the cable at once could cut signal continuity; leaving it grew the chance of sudden shorting.

Long-term, laying new cable in parallel, verifying section by section, and handing over the data flow was the most predictable course.

But independent measurement before and after the switch was needed, so the old colony's corrections were never mistaken for the new line's performance.

The final removal time was decided by human managers from corrosion rate, detour capacity, and record-continuity verification — not by the colony's state.

/hostile_groups/21/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: In facilities the Dead-Battery Metal Colony settled, the zones where metal dissolved away and the zones where metal returned as crystal fell clearly apart. Around spent-battery pouches and solder dross the surface pitted gray-white, while on ceramic edges a few meters away copper resin and nickel shells layered thick. This separation was made by invisible potential difference and capillary moisture.

/hostile_groups/21/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Dead-Battery Metal Colony's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G22E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/21/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/21/lifecycle.en: 1 electrolyte salt crystal nuclei → 2 dendritic growth along the pores → 3 the wet film touching the power bus and shielding mesh → 4 the precipitation path guided into the ceramic recovery tank → 5 neutralization to carbonate then powdering. Growth was bound to potential difference and capillary moisture.

/hostile_groups/21/senses.en: Growth speed shifted with local potential difference, electrolyte concentration, and dehumidifier-fan vibration. It recognized no document contents and was no agent tracking power stability.

/hostile_groups/21/dossier_prose.en:
In facilities the Dead-Battery Metal Colony settled, the zones where metal dissolved away and the zones where metal returned as crystal fell clearly apart.

Around spent-battery pouches and solder dross the surface pitted gray-white, while on ceramic edges a few meters away copper resin and nickel shells layered thick.

This separation was made by invisible potential difference and capillary moisture.

The colony's base film was thin like damp dust.

The micro-pores inside held electrolyte, and the insulating organic film slowed water draining away all at once.

Metal ions moved along this film, but the colony as a whole set no direction.

Only the crystal growth rate differed by the potential, humidity, ion concentration, and temperature measured at each point.

Recovery facilities usually consisted of porous alumina bricks, exchangeable graphite plates, and tin-plated collection mesh.

Setting the bricks' pore sizes differently by zone made a moisture gradient, and holding the mesh's potential slightly lower than the surrounding structure made copper and nickel precipitate there first.

Raising voltage gave fast yield but also steeply raised the chance of dendrites crossing insulation gaps.

So skilled teams adjusted humidity before voltage.

Lowering the condensation plates' temperature and changing the ceramic wicks' length folded the ion paths slowly into the recovery tank.

In work that used no building distribution net, movement was induced only by separated sacrificial metal plates and concentration difference, and the residual charge of capacitors and uninterruptible power supplies was penned in separate discharge boxes.

An arc chain could start from a single fine dendrite.

When the first short evaporated the crystal, metal vapor and carbonized traces became the path of the next discharge, and adjacent terminals connected in turn.

Even with breakers working, charge left in the grounding net or shielding layers could carry short chains on, so stopping was never guaranteed without physical sectioning.

Structural corrosion was far quieter.

When copper collection mesh and iron anchors touched the same wet film, iron dissolved first and copper thickened.

Seen from the surface recovery looked good, but the cross-sections of rack fasteners and cable trays shrank from inside.

Load tests had to run separately from metal recovery volume, and the rebar potential under the ceramic recovery tanks kept being measured.

In record-keeping zones the electrical reference point itself was the object of preservation.

As metal piled on the shielding mesh the connectors' reference potential shifted, and readers could not tell normal signals from corrosion noise.

Even with files remaining, once the links of index keys, identity correspondence tables, and access histories broke, whose record it was could not be confirmed, so physical media and the attribution structure had to be protected together.

The field manager limited the colony's passive reactions with human measures — replacing sacrificial electrodes, installing ceramic drainage insulating partitions.

When the recovery tank saturated, the collection mesh was mechanically stripped off, and before new surfaces went in, the potential of the surrounding grounding and structure was matched again.

Late action had the clogged drains pushing moisture into the walls, making new galvanic pairs outside the recovery zone.

The final judgment usually took the form of abandoning one of two infrastructures first.

Permanently discharging the power modules kept the record environment but lost backup power; cutting the archive's pipes and shielding saved the power equipment but broke the records' long-term preservation conditions.

Either way, the cut faces had to be sealed with ceramic and non-conductive resin, removing detours for potential and moisture, before the next precipitation path could be controlled.

/hostile_groups/22/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The Cryo-Spore Film was a gray-white composite membrane clinging thinly to freezer panels and the seams of transport boxes and low-temperature piping. Its surface looked like matte vinyl, but its cross-section repeated hydrophilic polymer lattices, silica hollow fiber, and dormant spore layers. Its normal thickness was only a few millimeters, and its moisture-laden edges could swell to nearly three times that.

/hostile_groups/22/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Cryo-Spore Film's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G23E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/22/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/22/dossier_prose.en:
The Cryo-Spore Film was a gray-white composite membrane clinging thinly to freezer panels and the seams of transport boxes and low-temperature piping.

Its surface looked like matte vinyl, but its cross-section repeated hydrophilic polymer lattices, silica hollow fiber, and dormant spore layers.

Its normal thickness was only a few millimeters, and its moisture-laden edges could swell to nearly three times that.

The film's core action lay not in producing or absorbing heat but in changing its paths of movement.

As the temperature difference across its faces grew, some capillaries contracted and the share of in-plane paths through connected hollow fibers rose.

The result was less frontal heat leakage, but heat crowded into frames and bolt-adhesive boundaries, making unforeseen cold points and hot layers.

Where moisture was present a different reaction occurred.

The hydrophilic edges drew in condensate and swelled, quickly sealing small gaps.

Seen as airtightness alone it was useful, but when water behind the seal could not escape, thin ice pouches grew and pushed panel surfaces and packaging from inside.

Sensor divergence was the first sign to check when handling this film.

An infrared camera showed only the cold flat surface, while contact thermocouples read the heat riding the frames, and fiber optics inside the wall caught delayed changes behind the ice layer.

The three values differing did not at once mean one was broken; a map including sensor depth and heat-pulse arrival time had to be redrawn.

Defrosting ran in zones at low output.

Heating the surface all at once made the polymer skin and inner fiber layers expand at different speeds, making fine cracks.

When cracks opened, dormant spores fell as dry powder, so local exhaust, sealed particle collectors, and respiratory protection were needed.

Vibration made a damage path separate from thermal shock.

Repeated shear transmitted from compressors, portable freezers, stage lifts, and transport carts fatigued the viscoelastic adhesive layer from its edges.

Each vibration turned the lifted parts into air paths opening and closing, swinging sensor values and inviting the automatic controllers' excess cooling and needless defrosting.

In the field an aluminum decoy cooling plate, colder than the actual preserved goods, was set on the far side of the work.

Condensate and fallen spores were guided to gather on that plate first, then a dry anhydrous break of fixed width was made with molecular-sieve desiccant and dry nitrogen.

The cooling plate was replaced into a sealed vessel before saturating, and when the break's dewpoint rose, incision stopped.

When opening sealed packaging, the contents were not warmed to peel the film off.

The whole package went into a low-temperature glove tent; holding the inner preservation temperature, a thin fluororesist barrier plate was slid between outer skin and film to limit cutting depth.

Partially thawed moisture refreezing could press specimen vessels and tissue with ice lenses, so temperature history, more than the cut line, became the stopping criterion.

Management procedures presupposed no intent or promise of the film.

When the work leader adjusted heat-source placement, humidity, vibration transmission, exhaust volume, and sensor position, the film reacted passively to those physical conditions.

Safe recovery depended not on the surface looking quiet but on whether hidden heat layers had been checked, the anhydrous break held, and spore collection and freezing temperatures kept to the end.

/hostile_groups/23/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The first signs usually appeared not as biological movement but as facility anomalies. A steady pulsation sounded in suction tubes that should have been empty, the membrane of a decommissioned perfusion cassette slowly swelled, and the water level of floor drain traps rose and fell in time with pump starts. Wet tissue fragments set no direction of their own, but they blocked valve gaps or bridged electrodes and changed the machines' judgment conditions.

/hostile_groups/23/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Medical-Tissue Machine Swarm's common ecology responded passively to facility surfaces and the local environment. The G24E identifiers marked biomechanical variants whose movement and work functions had differentiated within that environment; they were not treated as one individual with the common film or the whole installation.

/hostile_groups/23/bestiary/command_scop.en: The common facility ecology had no command core. Even the coordinating individuals of the mobile variants reacted only within their assigned conduit or work section, and stood in for neither human facility authority nor unit command.

/hostile_groups/23/dossier_prose.en:
The first signs usually appeared not as biological movement but as facility anomalies.

A steady pulsation sounded in suction tubes that should have been empty, the membrane of a decommissioned perfusion cassette slowly swelled, and the water level of floor drain traps rose and fell in time with pump starts.

Wet tissue fragments set no direction of their own, but they blocked valve gaps or bridged electrodes and changed the machines' judgment conditions.

What the collective could sense was pressure, flow, conductivity, temperature, turbidity, and power state alone.

It distinguished no faces, posts, or requests.

Cases that looked like reactions to alarm tones were in fact driven by voltage changes or pump-stop signals arising in the same circuits.

The core actions were the five routines of washing, pressurization, perfusion, drainage, and preservation.

No routine could make a new order of its own; it followed the paths the sensor thresholds and wiring allowed under the supervision keys.

So in the field its actions could never be fully predicted.

Rather than deciding, one had to physically trace which input ran to which relay and valve.

Fluid isolation was reviewed before power cutoff.

With power down, force remained in elastic membranes, gravity head, and accumulators, and auxiliary batteries could sense flow change late.

The supply and recovery sides had to be locked separately, then the middle section depressurized into recovery bags, before piping could be separated safely.

Aerosolization risk grew when blocked lines were opened hastily.

Vents, sinks, and overflow drain traps in particular became bypass outlets of automatic pressure correction.

Workers checked gauges behind transparent shields and opened only one low-pressure recovery path at a time.

Record recovery was a separate engineering problem.

Corridor-net controllers judged damaged blocks as cleaning targets, and access from ordinary terminals could send modification signals back with queries.

An electrically isolated optical receiver let the original device keep running while blocking the automatic cleanup commands.

Capture of essential devices often began at shared docking rails and wet contacts.

Controllers mistook connected devices not as equipment for people but as additional pumps or storage.

On separation, power lines and fluid couplings were checked before communication lines, and nothing returned to its original position until an independent battery start test finished.

Supervision keys were not symbols of authority but physical parts limiting circuits.

Washing, drainage, and movement keys were shaped not to be inserted simultaneously, and each stage's completion was confirmed on separate gauges.

Coordination among field leads focused on which function to allow first, and the collective neither agreed with nor demanded payment for those decisions.

On finding unidentified tissue fragments, preservation and evacuation could demand the same equipment.

Holding low-temperature perfusion cut the service carrier's power and loading space; cutting preservation input sent the fragments into the waste flow.

Either way, pressure, fluid, and power records had to be handled as independent boundaries, and before turning the last key, one checked what default state the transport rails and passage doors would return to.

/hostile_groups/24/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: A light laid on the floor looked, from far off, like a dotted line announcing the refuge direction. Up close, each dot held six legs and a small loading box, and two files of chassis flowed in opposite directions along the broken cable racks. The Lantern-Ant Swarm, first woken in the Mapo coalition transmission gallery — did not move to light the dark.

/hostile_groups/24/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Lantern-Ant Swarm was not a living ancient organism but a lineage of pre-collapse work machines. The G25E identifiers marked models and derivatives split from existing chassis forms, and meant neither biological breeding nor natural evolution.

/hostile_groups/24/bestiary/command_scop.en: The machine controller adjusted only work sequence and return lines. It could form neither combat command nor human legal judgment, and the human watch's halt and approval orders took precedence.

/hostile_groups/25/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: The dead siding of the Gangnam Line's Changdong depot hummed first, and a few seconds later a metal knee slowly unfolded from deep inside the maintenance shed. Even after the dust settled, the bipedal heavy walker did not walk straight off. It pressed the floor with the pressure grid of its soles, lowered the counterweight behind its body, and proclaimed its work radius with three low-frequency roars.

/hostile_groups/25/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Fossil-Roar Swarm was not a living ancient organism but a lineage of pre-collapse work machines. The G26E identifiers marked machine types and derivatives split from existing chassis forms, and meant neither biological breeding nor natural evolution.

/hostile_groups/25/bestiary/command_scop.en: The machine controller adjusted only work sequence and return lines. It could form neither combat command nor human legal judgment, and the human watch's halt and approval orders took precedence.

/hostile_groups/26/bestiary/common_ecolo.en: From the end of the submerged stair fourteen rows of footplate marks turned upward. The Water Compact's sluice gallery had reported drainage finished, but the trilobite-form scout still groped the floor. The Deep-Trilobite Swarm was a lineage of biomimetic robots that before the collapse had taken charge of deep inspection of sluices, conduits, and sewers, and of flood rescue.

/hostile_groups/26/bestiary/variant_rela.en: The Deep-Trilobite Swarm was not a living ancient organism but a lineage of pre-collapse work machines. The G27E identifiers marked machine types and derivatives split from existing chassis forms, and meant neither biological breeding nor natural evolution.

/hostile_groups/26/bestiary/command_scop.en: The machine controller adjusted only work sequence and return lines. It could form neither combat command nor human legal judgment, and the human watch's halt and approval orders took precedence.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/정.en:
At the second-floor archive of the Ttukseom workshop, Jeong Gaon ran his eyes first over the date lines where the ink had dried.

He was the records auditor of the workshop council of the Sermon Registry State, and he called any colleague who treated a circulating verbal testament as the original "the forger's neighbor."

He grew up in the Seoul living sphere of Korean origin, and though his temperament read as cold, his fingertips always worked the seal cord.

The display name Jeong Gaon and the permanent identifier K092 were never renumbered in the batches that followed.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he built the habit of filing the general manager's three testaments and the maintenance log side by side in one ledger.

His ambition was to let the workshop council, not the Record Bureau's slow ratification, remain the subject of interpretation.

The pencil marks he left on the archive windowsill every night were a small promise to return to his family, and that promise became the prototype of his debt.

His colleagues called the ambition stubbornness, but Jeong Gaon did not burn misdated copies; he locked them in a separate box.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The duty claim of the Ttukseom Heat-Source House tried to borrow Jeong Gaon's signature column, but he recognized only the successor charter that kept real company names out of the text.

Audit rosters without rotation signatures never went up on the council wall, and the HC04 observer could demand only scheduled registration.

His place in the community was proven not by credentials but by records of sending sealed copies to both sides at once.

When a house window pushed a unilateral interpretation broadcast, he declared it void for want of a stamp.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
On the day of the collapse three different testaments arrived at the same hour.

Jeong Gaon locked the council vault and withheld his stamp until Choi Jiwoo's voice record arrived.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged testament was confirmed as the original and the auditor's post was sold off as a tool of the succession war.

Even after the alarm fell silent, he did not remove his gloves, the last line of the LOSS list still unread.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the vault key to the Record Bureau escort detail and seizing the forgery suspect first.

When a sealed request from the Korea Strait Theater landed on the council desk, the calculation changed.

Escorting the sealed copy to the end kept the workshop's right of interpretation alive but drained the night rotation staff; prioritizing the suspect let one house monopolize the reading.

The choice remained as K093-TURN, and reversing it stopped part of the Ttukseom work squads.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Even now Jeong Gaon kept the roll call and the ledger queue as records auditor of the Sermon Registry State.

His standing was maintained not by inheritance but by license, signatures, and observation logs.

Even when the Ttukseom Heat-Source House demanded exclusive state ownership, he refused and matched the Cast profile's present column with the ledger every week.

The archive door had changed to a two-key system, one key held by the council and the other by the Record Bureau's observation box.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/비.en:
The secret was the bundle of misdated copies he had locked in the separate box.

The guilt grew only between the rotation roster he had saved and the name of one apprentice he failed to call that night.

Publishing everything could break Ttukseom trust by one notch, so he left only a partial-disclosure procedure.

The SECRET key did not open without the simultaneous signatures of two observers.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/관.en:
The testament copy he passed to Yun Seorin was a contract, and the night he refined Han Somi's joint-governance wording was an alliance.

With Park Serin's house ledger there remained a rivalry of interpretation, reading different dates in the same sentence.

No relation ended in betrayal alone, and salvation had opened for both at the same sealed box.

The endpoint of the existing relation ledger stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B001-K092.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In act one Jeong Gaon met the simultaneous arrival of three testaments head-on again.

In act two he weighed the HC04 duty claim and the XT03 sealed request on one desk.

In act three he paid the price of the withheld stamp in the downtime of the workshop's work squads.

The arc identifier was fixed as STORY-B001-K092.

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α Jeong Gaon prioritized escorting the sealed copy and chose the continuity of public interpretation.

In ending β he prioritized tracing the forgery suspect and protected his personal survival and the secret box.

Neither deleted the Sermon Registry State's slot among the sixteen states; only the branch split as K093-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day followed the turning-point record as either escort protection or forgery pursuit.
