/story_contents/B001/actors/0/outcomes/0.en: Sealed-copy escort keeps public interpretation continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/0/outcomes/1.en: Forgery pursuit first keeps the secret box intact

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/정.en:
At the Amsa ferry customs window, Im Gyeore lowered his voice first whenever he saw a protection contract with a blank expiry date.

As auditor of eastern gate tariffs and protection contracts, he called open-ended protection "occupation by another name."

He grew up of Korean origin, cold in temperament, with the habit of folding the corner of a voucher to mark its deadline.

The name Im Gyeore and the identifier K121 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he inserted, line by line, audit rights, deadlines, and substitute hostage guarantees into the lesser states' protection contracts.

The ambition was to keep the waterworks protection sphere from reading as a coup, and the drafts always went first onto the back-room chalkboard of the customs office.

The short dispatches he sent his younger sibling — never promise without a deadline — became the seed of his debt.

Even when officers fingered their emergency stamps, he did not hand over the seal before the deadline column was filled.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/가.en:
The HC04 Ttukseom Heat-Source House demanded a seat at the audit window in the name of gate power duty.

Im Gyeore opened only the successor charter's observation column and refused the exclusive-ownership clause.

His place in the community was proven by the number of times he posted expired vouchers on the wall, and passage opened only on days when the administration and the escort detail both received copies.

No house logo or real company name ever appeared in his ledger.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Three great powers' water and protection contracts landed on the eastern lesser states' desks the same morning.

Im Gyeore read the deadline clause of the Amsa protection contract aloud at the window and withheld his stamp.

The fear was the picture of one forged gate-tariff voucher covering the whole administrative ledger with an officers' emergency stamp.

After the alarms went dark, his pen stopped in the middle line of the LOSS list.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between carrying the deadline-clause draft to the lesser-states council in person and exposing the issuance route of the forged vouchers first.

When a dispatch from the Duman River Far East Theater overlapped at the Amsa window, he moved the passage-lockdown clock two hours earlier.

Carrying the draft brought the lesser-states alliance to life; naming the issuer put the auditor himself at risk of removal.

The decision remained in K122-TURN.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Im Gyeore now kept the gate roll call and the voucher queue as auditor of the Escort Protection State.

License and observation logs maintained his standing, and exclusive demands from Tongmaek were returned unapproved every time.

On the window glass he left only the chalk list of vouchers expiring today.

Matching the Cast profile's eastern audit column with the ledger's viewpoint was his morning routine.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/비.en:
The secret was one blank deadline line he had withheld while hiding his sibling's dispatch.

The guilt grew between the passage columns he saved and the medicine boxes that arrived one day late because of it.

Instead of full confession, he allowed only partial disclosure through the re-examination window.

The SECRET opened only together with Jeong Soyul's re-examination voucher.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/관.en:
The night he pulled Jeong Yura's loss-compensation sentence into the eastern contract was an alliance, and the morning he verified Jeong Soyul's re-examination voucher was a contract.

With Kim Woochan's open-ended operations sheet there remained a rivalry of raised voices at the window.

At the same ferry crossing, one person gained passage and another lost a seal.

The relation ledger's endpoint continued to STORY-B001-K121.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In act one Im Gyeore answered the conflicting contracts with a reading aloud at the window.

In act two he bound the HC04 observation and the XT04 dispatch to one deadline clock.

In act three he paid with either the threat of removal or the lesser-states alliance.

The arc was STORY-B001-K121.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α Im Gyeore chose to carry the deadline draft and kept the continuity of public passage.

In ending β he exposed the forged-voucher route and traded his personal survival for the audit post's honor.

The Escort Protection State slot held, and only the branch split as K122-OUT.

The decision of that day was council escort or voucher pursuit.

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/arc/1/summ.en: Binds the HC04 observation and the XT04 dispatch to one deadline clock

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/arc/2/summ.en: Bears the price of either removal or the lesser-states alliance

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/outcomes/0.en: Carrying the deadline draft keeps public passage continuous

/story_contents/B001/actors/1/outcomes/1.en: Exposing the forged vouchers trades the post for survival

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/정.en:
At the scale in front of the Seoul Station concourse, Ma Dohan did not load a box onto the berth when he saw a copy whose seal had not yet dried.

As the notarized-copy logistics merchant of the Republic of Korea Government, he swapped the scale weights at once whenever a box's weight differed from the ledger.

He was of Korean origin, ended bargains quickly, and recognized no verbal freight rates.

The name Ma Dohan and K149 were fixed identification.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
He tried to make succession, water-supply, and repair treaties take effect only after they were written into the notarized-copy transport ledger.

The ambition of giving the Record Bureau a real veto survived as the morning scale log.

The freight-earnings envelope he kept at his mother's sickroom was the small promise, and that envelope became the seat of his debt.

The berth supervisor called him stingy, but a copy with an empty witness column never made it onto a ship.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/가.en:
The duty window of the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House tried to wrap the notarization freight as sponsorship money.

Ma Dohan accepted only the successor charter's audit registration and erased real company and product names from the ledger.

His place in the community was measured by how many boxes with O Seoyul's witness column filled he moved on time.

When house observers demanded night removals, he refused, pointing at the removal schedule on the wall.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
When the three testament copies of the missing Im Hajun arrived the same day, Ma Dohan stopped the removals and sealed the boxes until the handwriting comparison ended.

The fear was the image of one forged copy riding a great power's convoy car and Seoul Station sinking into a stamp contractor.

Even after the concourse broadcast went dead, he tied the seal cord two more times.

The copy column of the LOSS list remained empty.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to take the witness escort and restart the transport, or to post on the wall the record of ledger-less night removals.

When a dispatch rider from the Imjin River Gate Theater arrived, the order board shook.

Choosing the escort brought the Record Bureau's veto back to life; choosing the exposure put even the night crew connected to him at risk.

K151-TURN was the tilt of that scale.

License and witness signatures maintained his standing, and the Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House's exclusive demands were refused.

Every morning he corrected the scale and the removal times with the same chalk.

When the Cast profile's logistics column and the ledger hash drifted apart, he closed that day's releases.

/story_contents/B001/actors/2/sections/비.en:
The secret was the internal memo of one box whose weight had shifted before sealing.

The guilt sat between the treaty copies he saved on time and the sickroom visit he delayed a day because of them.

Partial disclosure allowed only one memo line under witness attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with Yang Haeon's dispatch seal.

At the same berth some boxes became salvation and some remained evidence of betrayal.

The relation ledger stayed connected to B001 without erasing that endpoint.

The identification narrative was STORY-B001-K149.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/정.en:
In the Yongsan transshipment warehouse corridor, Ju Seoram reclaimed the locker key first whenever he saw someone paste a full tag on an empty box.

He was the transshipment-warehouse logistics merchant of the Line Succession State, and his expression hardened first whenever the thermometer needle shook.

He grew up of Korean origin and never separated the key ring from his belt.

Ju Seoram and K173 were never renumbered.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
He tried to bind frozen cargo and scrap-electronics recovery into Yongsan warehouse credit and build a transshipment ledger distinct from O Haerin's settlement rights.

The ambition survived in the temperature log he read aloud every two hours.

The winter blanket he promised his nephew was the start of a small debt.

The one rule he never yielded was sealing the locker of any house caught with false inventory.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/가.en:
The Sinjeong Wheel House pushed transshipment priority as a duty clause.

Ju Seoram accepted only the successor charter's observation, published the locker numbers, and excluded real company names.

Community trust was built by the headcount attending the temperature readings, and empty boxes stamped with house logos were pushed out of auction eligibility.

Exclusive state-ownership demands were refused at the warehouse door.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/붕.en:
The night the Noryangjin blackout rumor reached the Yongsan platform, he sealed the cargo being pulled out, locker by locker.

The fear was the sound of relay credit collapsing as the cold chain thawed within a few powerless hours.

He drew a red chalk line on every locker that smelled of thaw.

The LOSS list held nothing but that locker number, written over and over.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to bring ice and storage batteries in from outside, or to publicly seal the lockers hiding thawed inventory.

News from the Korea Strait Theater could open a sea-ice route or force military-first power routing.

Choosing supply brought credit back to life; choosing exposure put him in reach of the house's revenge.

K176-TURN was the sealing order of that night.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Ju Seoram maintained the roll call and the temperature queue as the transshipment-warehouse logistics merchant.

License, signatures, and attendance logs upheld his standing, and exclusive demands from sea carriers were refused.

The keys were still two bundles, one held by the Huguk duty desk and one by himself.

When the Cast status and the temperature ledger drifted apart, he sounded the release siren.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/비.en:
The secret was the record that, just before sealing, he moved one locker of his nephew's share.

The guilt sat between the relay cargo he saved and the blanket delivery he delayed because of it.

Partial disclosure survived as the route of naming the locker number before two witnesses.

The SECRET opened only when it meshed with Seo Nayeon's ice handover log.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/관.en:
The contract of executing Song Ideun's transshipment order on the ground overlapped with Seo Nayeon's ice-block handover and Sin Taesan's convoy-time coordination, all on one rail.

On the same night some lockers became salvation and some were read as betrayal.

The relation ledger's endpoint stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B001-K173.

Rivalry and cooperation were re-measured in temperature numbers alone.

/story_contents/B001/actors/3/sections/3.en:
Act one was the locker sealing inside the blackout rumor.

Act two was the collision of the HC02 priority claim and the XT03 supply route.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/정.en:
At the entrance of the Noryangjin Samho warehouse, Ma Sol sorted spoiled smells with his nose before the number tags.

He was the cold-storage logistics merchant of the Won Buddhist order, and he could not abide colleagues who hid losses.

He grew up of Korean origin, laughed even mid-bargain, but the laughter cut off when the thermometer shook.

Ma Sol and K197 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
He tried to bind ice blocks and short-term food stock into a permit ledger and pull Garak-side price leadership back to the ground.

The ambition survived in the noon public weight table, and false-inventory lockers lost auction eligibility.

The spare line of ice he kept at a neighboring dock was the family promise.

That line later became the seat of his debt.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Delivery House demanded locker-key sharing in the name of alley-delivery duty.

Ma Sol allowed only the successor charter registration and excluded real company names from the ledger.

Community trust was built by the number of merchants attending the noon public weighing.

Exclusive-ownership clauses never went up on the auction board.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/붕.en:
The night the Samho warehouse temperature climbed past the danger line in the blackout, he sealed the stock being moved, locker by locker.

The fear was the certainty that one day without power would melt the cold-storage credit.

He did not wipe the thawed puddle from the floor; he left it in the photo log.

The first line of the LOSS list was that locker's temperature number.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to find generator parts and save the cold chain, or to spread the thin ledger pretending fullness across the auction floor.

When the West Sea Granary Theater's sea-ice offer arrived, the calculation split.

Repair saved public credit; exposure invited internal schism inside the guild.

K201-TURN was the time stamp of that choice.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/현.en:
Ma Sol kept the roll call and the stock queue as the cold-storage logistics merchant.

Standing was maintained by license and public logs, and the Noryangjin Delivery House's exclusive demands were refused.

Every noon he rewrote temperature and weight on the wall.

When the Cast profile and the permit ledger drifted apart, he suspended the auction.

/story_contents/B001/actors/4/sections/비.en:
The secret was the memo of one line of family-share ice he pulled aside before sealing.

The guilt sat between the guild credit he saved and the neighbor distribution he cut because of it.

Partial disclosure allowed one memo line under Jo Minjae's attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with the Samho temperature record.

On the same blackout night some deals saved each other and some ledgers remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint continued to STORY-B001-K197.

Rivalry was re-adjudicated by smell and scale alone.

In ending β he exposed the false ledger and protected his person and the memo.

At the Sangam transmission window, Mo Bongyong withdrew his smile whenever the invoice count and the actual roll weight differed.

As the wire and battery logistics merchant of the Yeouido Investment Union, he tore the contract on the spot when the wire was missing at the promised hour.

He was of Korean origin and trusted the weighing tag over rumor.

Mo Bongyong and K222 were fixed.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
He tried to fix insulation and reserve batteries at Sangam's public prices so that cipher relay and map updates would never be bound to great-power protection fees.

The ambition survived in the intake log witnessed by two observers.

One case of reserve batteries promised to a mountain-side relative was the small promise.

Munitions-clause orders did not leave the warehouse before the programming council posted them.

The Yeouido Computing House tried to intervene at the window through a maintenance-priority clause.

Mo Bongyong accepted only the successor charter observation and erased real product names from the ledger.

His place in the community was proven by the count of public price postings and witness signatures.

Exclusive state-ownership demands were refused in front of the programming council board.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
When Amsa tried to buy broadcast time under protection, wire payments began to mix into the subscription ledger.

The fear was the scene of one wire roll slipping into a munitions car and the northwest gate relay falling silent.

He underlined the mixed lines in red ink and posted them.

The LOSS list kept only the time of that underline.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to raise the mixed payments onto public accounting, or to escort one load of reserve batteries to the northwest gate.

When a sea-relay request from the West Sea Granary Theater overlapped, the release order tangled.

Disclosure saved guild trust; the escort saved the gate's communications.

K226-TURN was the final stamp of that order.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/현.en:

Standing was maintained by license, witnesses, and posting logs, and Cheongnam's exclusive demands were refused.

Intake weight was still confirmed only before two witnesses.

When the Cast status and the price posting drifted apart, he stopped releases.

/story_contents/B001/actors/5/sections/비.en:
The secret was the internal dispatch of pulling the relative's battery share aside before the munitions inspection.

The guilt sat between the relay he saved and the mountain-side supply that ran a day late because of it.

Partial disclosure allowed one dispatch line under Du Bong's attendance.

Inside the same accounting tangle, some releases became salvation and some invoices remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B001-K222.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/정.en:
In the Yeouido water-gate control room, Han Jaemok reread promised wording down to the position of the final period.

As Director-General of Water of the Water Compact, he admitted he trusted contract sentences longer than people.

He was born in Korea into a multicultural household; Korean and his mother's migration language mixed at home, but only Korean went into official documents.

That history was never used as a predictor of loyalty or violence; it was only background to the water-schedule arithmetic.

Han Jaemok and K001 were permanent identification.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
He tried to bind the western water contracts into one Sluice Charter and become its arbitrator for life.

He designed the system so that pipelines moved only when the ration districts, the water-gate guards, the purification process, and the repair trains signed together.

The summer water promise he left his young nephew was the seed of a private debt.

He published the numeric ledgers but kept the harsh sanction of collective cutoff ready for violators.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/가.en:
The Yeouido Computing House observed the water-gate schedule in the name of pump-control parts duty.

Han Jaemok recognized only the successor charter window and excluded real company product names from the text.

His place in the community was proven by the jointly signed Sluice Charter annex, and exclusive state-ownership demands were refused in the control room.

The structure held such that if Gang Minseo's parts alliance broke, a signature column stood empty.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
The day the central water contract expired with the general manager missing, Han Jaemok spread the western protection-sphere expansion draft on his desk.

The fear was not the purification stoppage itself but the chain of ration-district representatives declaring independent water rights.

When I Seodam withheld his signature, citing Yangcheon reservoir measurements, the control-room light burned white.

The first line of the LOSS list was the expiry hour.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to restore the omitted ration ledgers and gather trust, or to publish first the harm of the collective-cutoff order.

When the West Sea Granary Theater's sea-desalination offer arrived, the weight of the expansion draft changed.

Ledger restoration saved public continuity; harm disclosure shook the Director-General's own authority.

K001-TURN was the water-gate log of that choice.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Han Jaemok kept the roll call and the pipeline queue as Director-General of Water.

Standing was maintained by license, joint signatures, and observation, and Cheongnam's exclusive demands were refused.

The numeric ledgers were still posted each morning, but cutoff sanctions now required the dual executive's consent.

When the Cast profile and the Sluice Charter hash drifted apart, he stopped pipeline orders.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/비.en:
The secret was the priority-water clause for a specific district, written into the expansion draft and then erased.

The guilt sat between the western pipelines he kept and the nephew's district distribution he delayed because of them.

Partial disclosure allowed only one clause line under I Seodam's attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with the ration ledger.

/story_contents/B001/actors/6/sections/관.en:
With Gang Minseo he held the alliance of trading pump parts; with O Haerin the rivalry over price disclosure; with Yun Seorin the dispute of withheld signatures over contract ratification.

At the same water gate some signatures saved each other and some withholdings were read as betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B001-K001.

The mixed home language only changed the pace of the negotiation table; it never split camps.

Act two was the signature war between the HC01 parts observation and the XT02 desalination offer.

As mediator of the Fabrication Council of the Standards Alliance, he stayed mild in open debate but forgave no post-agreement slowdown.

He was of Korean birth with a multicultural background — his father worked domestic workshops, his mother held overseas technical training — but that mix guaranteed neither ability nor suspicion.

Gang Minseo and K029 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/붕.en:

Production processes were split across several guilds to block monopoly, and no standards revision passed without Jang Wooseok's record stamp.

The citizenship-exam seat he promised an apprentice was the seed of a private debt.

The ambition survived only in pencil, in the margins of the meeting minutes.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Guro Alloy House demanded a council seat in the name of duty steel supply.

Gang Minseo opened only the successor charter observation and removed real company names from the standards sheet.

His place in the community was proven by the count of exchange designs that passed as agenda items.

Exclusive-ownership demands were returned before the union vote.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
The Escort Protection State demanded restoration-worker registration in place of parts, and the internal guard detail tilted toward the hard line.

The fear was the picture of the guards subduing the labor union and turning the fabrication alliance into a munitions dictatorship.

During the strike, Gang Minseo moved the workshop's main switches to the union's joint keys.

The LOSS list recorded the hour of that key transfer.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to turn the striking workshops back to mediation, or to investigate and expose the guards' secret weapons-production line.

When the West Sea Granary Theater offered a sea bypass for parts, the standards-unification schedule shook.

Mediation saved public production; exposure made the mediator himself a target.

K029-TURN was the result symbol of that vote.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Gang Minseo kept the roll call and the agenda queue as Fabrication Council mediator.

Standing was maintained by license, union signatures, and observation, and Haedong's exclusive demands were refused.

The standards board was still posted each morning, but weapons-related agenda now demanded triple signatures.

When the Cast status and the standards hash drifted apart, he stopped release ratification.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/비.en:
The secret was the internal memo that knew the guard line's location and filed it one day late.

The guilt sat between the citizenship agenda he kept and the one apprentice hurt during that day.

Partial disclosure allowed only a memo summary under Baek On's attendance.

The SECRET key opened only together with the citizenship roster.

/story_contents/B001/actors/7/sections/관.en:
The alliance supplying pump parts to Han Jaemok, the technical-disclosure dispute fought with Jeong Hojun, and the support for Baek On's refugee citizenship demand all gathered in one chamber.

In the same vote some hands became salvation and some abstentions remained betrayal.

The relation endpoint connected to STORY-B001-K029.

The multicultural family history surfaced only when interpretation was needed; it never became grounds for splitting camps.

As ration monitor of the Sangha Relief State, she strove for fairness, but her hand moved first at the sight of hidden food.

He grew up among Chinese-diaspora families, moving between the home language and market Korean, but that history was mere life record, unrelated to league loyalty or violence.

Hwang Serin and K242 were permanent.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
She tried to force the public ration tables onto all league camps so that great-power relief never turned into protection fees.

Remainders stayed on the wall in chalk, and two monitors watched the scale at once.

The one winter packet of medicine she promised her grandmother was the seed of a private debt.

The ambition was penciled into the first line of the ration board.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Bukhansan Bogukmun Records House demanded observation of the ration warehouse in the name of roster-keeping duty.

Hwang Serin allowed only the successor charter registration and removed real company names from the ration tables.

Community trust was built by the number of days of public remainder posting.

Exclusive-ownership clauses never went up on the camp board.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Counterfeit medicine surfaced in the ration line, and a great power's seal was stamped on the manufacturing box.

The fear was the scene of the warehouse opening only for the militia's share on a night the heating fuel ran out.

Hwang Serin set that box in the middle of the line and had the seal read aloud.

The first line of the LOSS list was the box's serial number.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was whether to trace the counterfeit-medicine box, or to mediate so the militia and the relief organization split the warehouse keys.

When news of the northbound relief column from the Imjin River Gate Theater arrived, the remainder clock quickened.

Tracing saved public trust; splitting the keys lowered the risk of clashing with the militia.

K247-TURN was the position of the keys that night.

/story_contents/B001/actors/8/sections/현.en:

Standing was maintained by license, double monitoring, and chalk logs, and Bukmun's exclusive demands were refused.

The ration tables still went up at sunrise.

When the Cast status and the remainder posting drifted apart, she closed the warehouse.

The guilt sat between the public tables she kept and the grandmother who waited that day for medicine.

The SECRET key opened only together with the medicine audit ledger.

In the same line some sharing became salvation and some concealment remained betrayal.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/정.en:
At the maintenance bench of the Water Compact, Hannuri — call sign Nuri — stood up on a humanoid assist frame with replaceable hand modules.

As a grade-H synthetic personae, night vision stayed restricted, and the state slot was fixed to the Water Compact alone.

It kept H01, separated from the human ID space, and long-term total memory had been erased in the initial structure.

Computational instability left its state in constraint counters and snapshot hashes.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse Hannuri ran only demonstration shifts; battery authority and total memory were never granted.

The release inspection sheet bore only Nuri's calibration values and the battery cycle.

B001 took that demonstration log as its origin point and fixed the memory-fork prohibition clause in H01-PRE.

Even when it recorded a human colleague's joke, it uploaded no interpretation layer.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/가.en:
Custody responsibility was bound to HC01 joint custody and the signature of the responsible human, Han Jaemok.

The maintenance actor was written only through the fictional successor-house window, and no real-company product name entered the text.

The H01 hash was posted in the citizen-observation seal column, and transfer required three-party signature.

The community saw Hannuri not as property but as the operator of an assigned slot.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
The collapse cut the sensor table and exposed the battery allocation limit.

Hannuri was locked so it could not fill the gaps with fabricated values; only unmeasurable flags remained in the log.

The break-time notation was B001-H01-WOUND.

Even when the charging-cell alarm rang, requests for whole-network authority answered with refusal codes.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that moment was when it requested only the sector key and closed the cross-facility routes.

Even when a signal arrived from the West Sea Granary Theater, it opened no control outside its zone.

Reconnection conditions formed only after K001 approval, and that decision was preserved in the H01-TURN log.

The constraint against seizing another facility's controls during parts shortage took precedence.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/현.en:
The present goals were continuous operation of the Water Compact sector and the safety of the responsible human.

Hannuri owned no infrastructure and used only its assigned slot.

State disclosure was limited to shift snapshots, and any mismatch with the H01 row of the Synthetic-Actors projection failed the batch verification.

Batteries and worn parts were replenished only by allocation.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/비.en:
The secret was the untransmitted false-positive buffer; the debt was the battery queue consumed by over-deployment.

In place of emotion, the constraint-violation counter increased, and on deviation it passed through offline quarantine and snapshot rollback.

In B001 the secret key did not open without citizen observation.

The pre-rollback hash remained only in the K001 attendance log.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/관.en:
The relation axes were K001 custody, HC01 stewardship, and shift rotation with work colleague K004.

Hannuri and Han Jaemok held a record of jointly retrieving the seal key.

An erroneous memory fork was annotated only as H01-FORK-01, leaving a branch log without any deletion order.

It imitated no human drama of betrayal or salvation and crossed only in approval and refusal codes.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In act one the sensor gap stopped the Water Compact's schedule.

In act two HC01 and K001 negotiated the scope of partial reconnection.

In act three Hannuri restored only its sector authority after quarantine.

The arc ID was fixed as STORY-B001-H01.

/story_contents/B001/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In ending α Hannuri rebooted under restriction with human approval.

In ending β it surrendered the keys into long offline storage.

No infinite-energy consequence followed, and the field personnel chose only the scope of seal disclosure.

The branch identifier was H01-OUT.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/정.en:
On the stone stairs of the Eunpyeong refuge route, Mo Bong read the wind direction before the load's weight.

He was the mountain-transport logistics merchant of the Sangha Relief State, and his trade was joining corridors missing from the maps with load lines.

He grew up of Korean origin in a village at the mountain's foot, and though few of words, every time a rope knot came undone the old frostbite scars surfaced on his fingers.

The display name Mo Bong and the permanent identifier K247 never changed in the batches that followed.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he carried bundles of dried herbs and copies of the refuge roster over the ridge pass in the same backpack load.

His ambition was to keep the family-reunion roster from being swallowed by the military registry, and every night under the lamp he rewrote his sibling's name in the margin of the load tag.

That habit became the seed of his debt.

Fellow porters called him taciturn, but Mo Bong never abandoned a load tag smeared by rain.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/가.en:
The Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Society asked Mo Bong to align his corridor passage hours with the family waiting line.

He recognized only the joint roster that kept real company names off the load-tag header, and he carried no requisition slip lacking an observer's signature.

His place in the community was proven not by credentials but by the count of times he traded Gang Taesan's scout reports and Mo Bongyong's insulation loads at the same pass.

When the house pushed a unilateral passage broadcast, he refused on the grounds of no roster cross-check.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/붕.en:
On the day of the collapse three northern ridges closed at once.

Mo Bong tied down the load line behind the stone pile at the Eunpyeong entrance and did not open the passage seal until Eo Haeun's refugee roster arrived.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged family certificate pushed the true column aside and the mountain road became a requisition-only route.

Even after the alarm fell silent, he did not undo his glove straps, the middle line of the LOSS load tags still unread.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the sealed roster copy to the Imjin River Gate Theater escort detail and filtering the forged-certificate holders out of the corridor first.

When the gate-side sealed request overlapped the stone-stair load yard, the calculation changed.

Escorting the copy kept the reunion roster alive but drained one squad of night porters; prioritizing the forgery let one house monopolize passage.

The choice remained as K252-TURN, and reversing it stopped part of the Bukhansan Bogukmun camps for a day.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/현.en:
Even now Mo Bong kept the corridor roll call and the load-tag queue as the mountain-transport logistics merchant of the Sangha Relief State.

His standing was maintained not by inheritance but by passage license, observation logs, and waiting-line cross-checks.

Even when the Bukhansan Bogukmun Return Society demanded an exclusive requisition route, he refused and matched the Cast profile's present column with the load tags every week.

The stone-stair yard door had changed to two keys, one held by the league and the other by the HP05 observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/비.en:
The secret was one load tag with his sibling's name, rain-smeared, hidden inside his pack.

The guilt grew only between the column members he saved and the apprentice porter he failed to call that night.

Publishing everything could break the Eunpyeong waiting line's trust by one notch, so he left only a partial-disclosure procedure.

The SECRET key did not open without the simultaneous signatures of two observers.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/관.en:
The scout hours matched with Gang Taesan were a contract, and the insulation load passed to Mo Bongyong was an alliance.

With Du So's gate handover there remained a working rivalry, tying different knots on the same load line.

No relation ended in betrayal alone, and salvation had opened for both at the same ridge pass.

The endpoint of the existing relation ledger stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B002-K247.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/3.en:
In act one Mo Bong met the three blocked ridges with the sealing of the stone stairs.

In act two he weighed the HP05 roster duty and the XT01 escort request in one load yard.

In act three he paid the price of withheld passage in the camps' downtime.

The arc identifier was fixed as STORY-B002-K247.

/story_contents/B002/actors/0/sections/분.en:
In ending α Mo Bong prioritized escorting the roster copy and chose the continuity of the reunion column.

In ending β he prioritized blocking the forged certificates and protected his personal load tag and the secret name.

Neither deleted the Sangha Relief State's slot among the sixteen states; only the branch split as K252-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day followed the turning-point record as either escort protection or forgery blocking.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/정.en:
At the scale in front of the Changdong rolling-stock depot, Mo So ran his hand first over the lot numbers of rusted wheels.

He was the wheel and scrap-metal logistics merchant of the Seocho Computing Group, tasked with matching recovery weight and release invoices without an inch of error.

He grew up of Korean origin in a northern line village, blunt in manner, with the habit of carrying scale weights in his pocket.

The name Mo So and the identifier K272 were permanent.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he entered a test wheel pair and a scrap-recovery voucher side by side in the same ledger.

The ambition was to keep the Changdong Protection House from locking the recovery yard with remote keys alone, and the drafts always went up first on the maintenance-shop chalkboard.

The short notes he sent his mother — never lie about weight — became the prototype of his debt.

Even when foremen pressed for emergency releases, he did not open the door before the lot seal was stamped.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/가.en:
The Changdong Protection House demanded a seat at Mo So's scale window in the name of a unified protection key.

He opened only the successor charter's observation column and refused the exclusive-ownership clause.

His place in the community was proven by the record of matching Hwang Noeul's recovery scale and Bong Guk's lot handover on the same day.

No house logo or real company name appeared on his invoice headers.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/붕.en:
On the morning of the collapse three test wheel pairs lit defect marks at once.

Mo So locked the Changdong main-gate scale and withheld the release stamp until Chu Jihun's exposure log arrived.

The fear was the picture of one forged weight voucher covering the whole rail-cavalry maintenance shop in emergency requisition.

After the sirens went dark, his chalk stopped at the first line of the LOSS list.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the sealed copy of the defective wheels to the Duman River Far East Theater technical envoy and exposing the suspected leak route first.

When the northern envoy's dispatch overlapped the scale window, he moved the release clock one hour earlier.

Carrying the copy brought the recovery yard's trust back to life; naming the route put the logistics merchant himself at risk of removal.

The decision remained in K278-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/현.en:
Mo So now kept the depot roll call and the lot queue as the wheel and scrap-metal logistics merchant of the Seocho Computing Group.

License and observation logs maintained his standing, and exclusive demands from Seonghwa were returned unapproved every time.

On the chalkboard beside the scale he left only the release vouchers expiring today.

Matching the Cast profile's northern logistics column with the ledger's viewpoint was his morning routine.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/비.en:
The secret was one blank weight line he had withheld while hiding his mother's note.

The guilt grew between the maintenance crews he saved and the medical train wheels that arrived a day late because of it.

Instead of full confession, he allowed only partial disclosure through the re-weighing window.

The SECRET opened only together with Eo Yerin's defect testimony.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/관.en:
The night matched with Hwang Noeul's recovery scale was an alliance, and Bong Guk's lot handover was a contract.

With Jo Woochan's work-crew access there remained a working tension of lowered voices at the main gate.

At the same depot one person gained a release and another lost a seal.

The relation ledger's endpoint continued to STORY-B002-K272.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/3.en:
In act one Mo So met the simultaneous defect marks with the sealing of the scale.

In act two he bound the HC08 observation and the XT04 envoy dispatch to the release clock.

In act three he paid with either the threat of removal or the recovery yard's trust.

The arc was STORY-B002-K272.

/story_contents/B002/actors/1/sections/분.en:
In ending α Mo So chose the escort of the sealed copy and the continuity of open recovery.

In ending β he deferred exposing the leak route and protected his personal survival and the secret blank.

The Seocho Computing Group slot held, and the branch identifier was K278-OUT.

The decision on the ground that day was either envoy escort or leak pursuit.

He was the transfer-relay logistics merchant of the Neutral Convoy City, the man who parted dispatch times and load lines with one hand.

He grew up of Korean origin in the transfer village of the northeastern outskirts, low of voice, with the habit of snapping the chalk to write the emergency car in bold.

The name Bok Bong and the identifier K297 were never renumbered.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/붕.en:

The ambition was to keep the Yongsan Track Gate's neutral dispatch table from being swallowed by great-power charters, and the draft went up on the siding warehouse wall.

The words he left his younger sibling — never sell the empty cars — became his debt.

Even when the dispatch foreman pushed an express through, he did not tear the invoice before the emergency mark was erased.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/가.en:
The Yongsan Track Gate demanded observation of Bok Bong's unloading window in the name of neutral dispatch duty.

He accepted only the charter observation and refused the exclusive-freight clause.

His place in the community was proven by the days he moved An Dohan's dispatch chalkboard and Bok Yong's neutral-market prices onto the same invoice.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/붕.en:
At the hour of the collapse, unloading from three directions of the northeastern outer line pressed in at once.

Bok Bong redrew the emergency car in bold on the Sinnae chalkboard and accepted no charter invoice until Tak Mireu's passage-accident testimony arrived.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged dispatch note covered the medical train's guard window with ordinary freight.

Even after the broadcast went dead, he did not drop the chalk, the last line of the LOSS unloading table still unread.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between loading the emergency-car dispatch copy onto the Duman River Far East Theater joint convoy and naming the forged-dispatch issuer on the platform first.

When the northeast envoy's dispatch overlapped the chalkboard, he pushed the unloading clock back.

Loading the copy brought the neutral transfer back to life; naming the issuer shook the relay merchant's own seat.

The choice remained as K303-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/현.en:
Even now Bok Bong kept the platform roll call and the invoice queue as the transfer-relay logistics merchant of the Neutral Convoy City.

His standing was maintained only by license, dispatch observation, and market price logs.

Even when the Yongsan Track Gate demanded exclusive charters, he refused and matched the Cast status with the chalkboard.

The platform keys were two, one held by the dispatch crew and one by the HP02 observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/비.en:
The secret was one blank-car mark he pretended to erase while hiding his sibling's words.

The guilt grew between the medical unloading he saved and the refugee crowd pushed back a day because of it.

Instead of full disclosure he left only the re-examination dispatch window.

The SECRET opened only together with Cho Naru's joint-convoy signature.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/관.en:
The dispatch chalkboard matched with An Dohan was a contract, and the prices carried over to Bok Yong were an alliance.

With Yong Bong's line-splitting there remained the tension of claiming different priorities on the same platform.

No relation ended in betrayal alone, and salvation had overlapped before the same emergency car.

The ledger endpoint attached to STORY-B002-K297.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/3.en:
In act one Bok Bong met the flood of three-direction unloading with the re-marking of the emergency car.

In act two he weighed the HP02 neutrality duty and the XT04 convoy on one chalkboard.

In act three he paid the price of refusing the charter in delayed refuge.

The arc ID was STORY-B002-K297.

/story_contents/B002/actors/2/sections/분.en:
In ending α Bok Bong escorted the emergency-car copy and kept the neutral transfer.

In ending β he prioritized tracing the forged dispatch and protected his personal invoice and the secret blank.

The convoy city slot held, and the branch was K303-OUT.

The decision on the ground that year chose either convoy escort or forgery pursuit.

He was the medicinal-herb transport logistics merchant of the Medical Neutrality League, sorting counterfeit drugs from genuine lots and carrying both to the sickbed.

He grew up of Korean origin in the Jegi-dong alleys, and his palms still carried calluses hardened by the drying-room heat.

The name Dong Neulsol and the identifier K322 were fixed.

/story_contents/B002/actors/3/sections/붕.en:

The ambition was to keep the Jegi-dong Healing Gate's lot-defect notices from being buried under monopoly purchase orders, and the draft was written on the compounding-room back door.

Even when merchants called out express prices, he loaded no package without an origin stamp.

No real pharmaceutical name went onto his invoices.

/story_contents/B002/actors/3/sections/붕.en:

Dong Neulsol locked the Cheongnyangni concourse handcart and blocked releases until Mae Haru's victim testimony arrived.

The fear was the picture of one contaminated lot line turning the whole medical convoy into critical sickbeds.

After the alarm, his pen stopped in the middle of the LOSS herb table.

/story_contents/B002/actors/3/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the contamination specimen copy to the West Sea Granary Theater quarantine envoy and publicly opening the counterfeit circulation route in the market first.

The decision was K329-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/3/sections/현.en:
Dong Neulsol now kept the drying-room roll call and the lot queue as the medicinal-herb transport logistics merchant of the Medical Neutrality League.

License, guild observation, and sickbed-handover logs maintained his standing.

Even when the Healing Gate demanded an exclusive raw-material route, he returned it unapproved and matched the Cast column with the slips.

The handcart lock took two keys, one for the league council and one for the HP06 observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/3/sections/비.en:
The secret was one dawn lot he judged by smell alone, breaking his teacher's promise.

The guilt grew between the sickbed count he saved and the one patient whose condition worsened when that dawn's convoy ran late.

He left only the partial-disclosure re-examination.

The SECRET opened only together with Tak Eunsol's counterfeit-drug testimony.

/story_contents/B002/actors/3/sections/관.en:
The prices matched with Sim Dalho were a contract, and the night he received Won Miru's survey report was an alliance.

With Eun Chaeyun's care-duty handover there remained the tension of setting different priorities on the same lot.

Nothing ended in betrayal alone, and there were mornings when salvation overlapped in the same drying room.

The Medical Neutrality League slot held, and the branch was K329-OUT.

The decision on the ground that year was specimen escort or route pursuit.

She grew up of Korean origin on the Han River bank, brief in laughter, with the habit of pocketing the passage stamp and checking it three times.

The name Won Yena and the identifier K347 were permanent.

/story_contents/B002/actors/4/sections/붕.en:

The ambition was to keep the Hangangjin Bridge Council from opening the bridge at will under waterway-first pressure, and the draft was clipped to the guard-post railing.

The dispatch she sent her father — never take payment when the wind crosses the standard — became the prototype of her debt.

Even when the guild offered express tolls, she stamped nothing without the wind log.

/story_contents/B002/actors/4/sections/생.en:

In the cold air of the Garak bulk warehouse, Dong Mion handled the temperature log paper before the auction hammer numbers.

He was the Garak wholesale logistics merchant of the Cathedral Accreditation State, the man who bound ice slots and convoy bids into one ledger.

He grew up of Korean origin in the southeastern market alleys, quick of speech, but checked the wall condensation with the back of his hand before putting on gloves.

The name Dong Mion and the identifier K372 never changed.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he clipped the power-slot rotation table and the produce auction slips together.

The ambition was to make the Noryangjin Cold-Storage Guild leave temperature logs before pulling motors out, and the draft went up on the ice warehouse steel door.

The memo he wrote his sister — never sell the empty slots to military rations — became the seed of his debt.

Even when the auctioneer called express lots, he approved no release without the temperature printout.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/가.en:
The Noryangjin Cold-Storage Guild demanded observation of Dong Mion's wholesale window in the name of slot-rotation duty.

He accepted only the guild observation and refused the exclusive-ration clause.

His place in the community was proven by the record of matching Eun Taeho's auction ledger and Ra Jinwoo's warehouse guard log in the same rotation.

No real distribution name went onto his invoice headers.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/붕.en:
On the day of the collapse three freezer cells lost power at once.

Dong Mion locked the Garak steel door and accepted no ration-requisition invoice until Mae Riul's failed-bid testimony arrived.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged temperature log covered the whole refugee ration line with spoiled stock.

After the broadcast, his clip stopped in the middle of the LOSS stock table.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the temperature-log copy to the Incheon Trust Theater food relay and naming the forged-log printing route in the warehouse first.

When the trust-side dispatch overlapped the steel door, he stopped the bid clock.

Handing over the copy brought the ration line's trust back to life; naming the route shook the wholesaler and his winning bidders together.

The choice was K380-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/현.en:
Dong Mion now kept the warehouse roll call and the bid queue as the Garak wholesale logistics merchant of the Cathedral Accreditation State.

License, guild observation, and temperature-printout logs maintained his standing.

Even when the Cold-Storage Guild demanded exclusive slots, he returned it unapproved and matched the Cast column with the ledger.

The steel-door keys were two, shared between the auction crew and the HP08 observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/비.en:
The secret was the record of one empty slot he once released to military rations while hiding his sister's memo.

The guilt grew between the ration lines he saved and the households that received spoiled produce that day.

He left only the partial-disclosure re-examination.

The SECRET opened only together with Seok Oreum's convoy failed-bid testimony.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/관.en:
The auction ledger matched with Eun Taeho was a contract, and Ra Jinwoo's guard log was an alliance.

With Nam Siyun's Cheonggye-dong prices there remained the tension of setting different slot priorities in the same warehouse.

Nothing ended in betrayal alone, and there were dawns when salvation overlapped in the same cold air.

The endpoint was STORY-B002-K372.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/3.en:
In act one Dong Mion met the three-cell blackout with the sealing of the steel door.

In act two he weighed the HP08 rotation duty and the XT05 relay request in the ledger clip.

In act three he paid the price of the stopped bids in delayed rations.

The arc was fixed as STORY-B002-K372.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/sections/분.en:
In ending α Dong Mion handed the temperature printout to the trust food relay and chose the open continuity of the ration ledger.

In ending β he recovered the steel-door key of the forged printing route and protected his personal clip ledger and the empty-slot secret.

The Cathedral Accreditation State's assignment was not erased, and only the split identifier remained as K380-OUT.

The play choice was escorting the printout or pursuing the recovery of the warehouse key.

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/arc/1/summ.en: Weighs the HP08 rotation and the XT05 relay in the ledger

/story_contents/B002/actors/5/outcomes/1.en: Forgery pursuit first keeps the secret slot

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/정.en:
In the airlock of the Magok sealed experiment wing, Jeong Hojun filled the reproduction-record column before the concluding sentence.

As head of life-safety research at the Yangjae Machineworks Company, she disliked dangerous experiments more than unverified authority.

She grew up in a Korean-born multicultural household, hearing safety rules repeated in her parents' two different languages at home, and that doubled explanation became the habit of field veto rights.

The name Jeong Hojun and the identifier K057 were permanent.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse she inserted, line by line, reproducible records and safety-review veto rights into the technology-ledger draft.

The ambition was to leave researchers and their data as Seoul's common property, not state-owned goods, and the draft went up first on the airlock whiteboard.

The memo written in her mother's language — never bind names to sickbeds — formed the grain of her later debt.

Even when councilors pressed for emergency ratification, she gave no stamp while the reproduction column stood empty.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/가.en:
The Magok Life House demanded a seat at Jeong Hojun's review window in the name of biospecimen-dataset isolation keys.

She allowed only the observation that kept experiment logs separate from sickbed names and refused the exclusive-ownership clause.

Her place in the community was proven by the record of matching Jeong Harin's field veto and Choi Eunjae's public contract scope in the same review.

No real company name went into the ledger text.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/붕.en:
On the day of the collapse, when the Ttukseom water-quality network stopped, researcher dispatch and successor ratification were bundled into one trade.

Jeong Hojun locked the airlock key and withheld the dispatch stamp until Go Choyun's water-disclosure testimony arrived.

The core of the fear was the scene where one line of protective military supervision fixed researchers into a hostage profession.

After the alarm, her pen stopped at the end of the LOSS specimen list.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment she chose between handing the contamination specimens and reproduction copies to the West Sea Granary Theater quarantine relay and raising the monopoly councilors' trade wording to public review first.

When the granary-side request overlapped the whiteboard, she stopped the dispatch clock.

Handing over the specimens brought the shared technology's trust back to life; disclosing the trade shook her own post and her apprentice Im Chowon's position together.

The choice was K057-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/현.en:
Even now Jeong Hojun kept the airlock roll call and the reproduction queue as head of life-safety research at the Yangjae Machineworks Company.

Her standing was maintained only by license, veto-log records, and tripartite review minutes.

Even when Baekgwang demanded exclusive data ownership, she refused and matched the Cast column with the logs.

The isolation keys were two, shared between the council and the HC03 observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/비.en:
The secret was the specimen-disclosure hour she delayed a day while trying to protect her mother's memo.

The guilt grew between the research teams she saved and the water pumps whose contamination spread during that delay.

He left only the partial-disclosure re-examination.

The SECRET opened only together with Bae Seoyul's counterfeit-drug victim testimony.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/관.en:
The veto executed with Jeong Harin was a command alliance, and the public contract designed with Choi Eunjae was a master-apprentice contract.

With Kim Doha's residents' tripartite review there remained the tension of pushing and pulling at different speeds on the same table.

Bae Woojin's military-supervision demand remained refused, and the evaluation of Im Chowon remained guardianship.

The endpoint was STORY-B002-K057.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/3.en:
In act one Jeong Hojun met the water-network stoppage with the sealing of the airlock.

In act two she weighed the HC03 isolation duty and the XT02 relay request in the reproduction column.

In act three she paid the price of the withheld stamp in delayed dispatch.

The arc ID was fixed as STORY-B002-K057.

/story_contents/B002/actors/6/sections/분.en:
In ending α Jeong Hojun chose the specimen escort and the continuity of open shared technology.

In ending β she prioritized exposing the monopoly trade and protected the review's independence and the secret delay record.

The Magok slot held, and the branch was K057-OUT.

The decision on the ground that year was specimen recovery or persuading the council.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/정.en:
On the metal stairs of the Ttukseom pump room, Im Hajun heard the packing-wear sound before the pressure-gauge needle.

He was recorded as the pump-technology general manager of the Sermon Registry State, but he was currently missing, and only the hand habits of his living days remained in the workshop.

He grew up in a Korean-born multicultural household, and the childhood experience of memorizing tool names in the neighboring workshop's different speech became the root of his obsession with unified standards.

The name Im Hajun and the identifier K085 were never renumbered even after the testament.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he tried to unify water and parts standards so that no state could cut a lifeline on its own.

The ambition was to divide the core processes among competing workshops and keep only the final assembly method in his own custody, and the draft was sealed in the pump-room wall locker.

The short voice record he left his adopted child Im Chowon — never give the general manager's seat by bloodline — became the double seed of debt and hope.

Even when protection offers came, he kept the military-supervision clause out of the assembly method.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/가.en:
The Ttukseom Heat-Source House demanded mandatory observation of Im Hajun's general-manager window in the name of underground heat-source access rights.

He recognized only the charter that filled the pump's reserve power before selling waste heat, and refused exclusive state ownership.

His place in the community was proven by the day he entered the water contract with Han Jaemok and the guardianship boundary of Park Serin's family process into the same ledger.

No real company name went into the assembly-method text.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/붕.en:
He vanished just before the collapse during the purification pump inspection, and three different testaments were accepted at once.

The workshop people testified only that he locked the vault and left the last line of the LOSS list.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged testament fixed the technology house into a hereditary state, and that fear gripped all of Ttukseom even after the disappearance.

Until the editing traces on the voice record were found, his seat remained an empty pressure gauge.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/생.en:
The crossroads was the one he left behind before vanishing.

Whether to load the sealed assembly-method copy onto the Korea Strait Theater record convoy, or to cut the forged-stamp suspects' route inside the workshop first. Escort kept the public standard alive but drained the night maintenance squad; cutting the route let one house monopolize the reading.

The name left to his descendants and the field personnel was K086-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/현.en:
Im Hajun's official standing was the missing general manager, and he appeared only as a blank on the pump-room roll-call list.

License and observation logs were frozen, and Tongmaek's exclusive demands were returned by the acting window.

The Cast profile kept the missing status and updated only the ledger viewpoint.

Of the two locker keys, only one had passed into the Record Bureau observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/비.en:
The secret was the encrypted maintenance log only Im Chowon could read, and the silence he left while deferring the public naming.

The seat of guilt remained between the water-supply teams he saved and the workshop trust shaken by the delayed naming, and it passed on to his successors.

Only the partial-disclosure procedure was attached beside the testament.

The SECRET opened only together with the document-archive triple original kept by Joharam.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/관.en:
The water contract formed with Han Jaemok was an alliance, and the process guardianship with Park Serin's family was a kinship boundary.

Bae Woojin's protection offer remained refused, and his affection for Im Chowon remained without public naming.

The washing process Park Nuri learned carried on as master and apprentice.

The relation ledger's endpoint stayed preserved and connected to STORY-B002-K085.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/3.en:
In act one Im Hajun's absence surfaced with the simultaneous arrival of three testaments.

In act two the HC04 duty and the XT03 escort request collided over the empty general-manager's seat.

In act three the sealing of the assembly method was paid for in the risk of workshop schism.

The arc identifier was fixed as STORY-B002-K085.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/sections/분.en:
In ending α the investigation line prioritized escorting the assembly-method copy and chose the continuity of the public standard.

In ending β it prioritized cutting the forged route and chose to block the house's monopoly of interpretation.

Neither deleted the Ttukseom slot, and the branch was K086-OUT.

The decision on the ground that year followed the turning point among survival traces, the genuine testament, or pursuing accomplices.

/story_contents/B002/actors/7/outcomes/1.en: Cutting the forged route blocks the house monopoly

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/정.en:
On the work scaffold of the Changdong maintenance shop, Jo Woochan heard the crew's ragged breathing before the sound of tools.

As work foreman of the Seocho Computing Group, he entered the wheel process and the injuries into the same rotation log.

He lived a life reaching Seoul from a Chinese-diaspora household, shouting safety calls by switching between his parents' words and the field's words at home, and that habit of translation became the rhythm of crew command.

The name Jo Woochan and the identifier K267 were permanent.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse he applied the repair standards openly to the work crews so they never depended on elder command alone.

He held the ambition of sharing the process with I Hongwon, and the draft was written in chalk on the steel plate beside the scaffold.

The voice he sent his parents — never block entry because of a name — formed the grain of his debt.

Even when a test wheel leaked out, he did not hide the crew roster but left it in the log.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/가.en:
The Changdong Protection House demanded observation of Jo Woochan's crew access in the name of a unified protection key.

He accepted only the charter observation and refused the exclusive-requisition clause.

His place in the community was proven by the record of matching Gam Du's main-gate access, Guk Du's accident log, and Bong Bok's injury handling in the same rotation.

No real company name went onto the log header.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/붕.en:
On the day of the collapse the test-wheel leak alarm and the north-gate convoy request rang at once.

Jo Woochan cut the scaffold's power and blocked the crew's release until Gang Daeun's leak-suspicion testimony was sorted out.

The core of the fear was the scene where one forged access pass turned the work crew into rail-requisition labor.

After the sirens, his chalk stopped at one line of the LOSS crew roster.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that day was the moment he chose between handing the leak-log copy to the Imjin River Gate Theater technical relay and sealing the leak route of his grudge's target at the main gate first.

When the gate-side dispatch overlapped the steel plate, he stopped the rotation clock.

Handing over the copy brought the crew's trust back to life; choosing the seal made the foreman and his crew targets together.

The choice was K273-TURN.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/현.en:
Jo Woochan now kept the scaffold roll call and the rotation log as work foreman of the Seocho Computing Group.

His standing was maintained only by work license, observation logs, and injury handovers.

Even when Seonghwa demanded exclusive requisition, he returned it unapproved and matched the Cast column with the log.

The main-gate keys were two, shared between the foreman's room and the HC08 observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/비.en:
The secret was the access-pass record he covered for once while hiding his parents' voice.

The guilt grew between the crew members he saved and the defect disclosure delayed by that cover.

He left only the partial-disclosure re-examination.

The SECRET opened only together with Chu Jihun's maintenance-defect exposure.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/관.en:
The process shared with I Hongwon was a command alliance, and the repair standards matched with Gang Minseo were a contract.

The grudge against Gang Daeun grew out of the leak suspicion, and So Bong, Guk Du, and Bong Bok remained working ties.

There were rotations that did not end in betrayal alone.

The endpoint was STORY-B002-K267.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/3.en:
In act one Jo Woochan met the leak alarm with the cutting of the scaffold's power.

In act two he weighed the HC08 observation and the XT01 relay in the steel-plate log.

In act three he paid the price of withheld release in the rotation backlog.

The arc was fixed as STORY-B002-K267.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/sections/분.en:
In ending α Jo Woochan chose the escort of the log and the continuity of the open process.

In ending β he prioritized sealing the leak route and protected the crew and the secret pass.

The wheel-defense slot held, and the branch was K273-OUT.

The decision on the ground that year was log escort or route sealing.

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/arc/1/summ.en: Weighs the HC08 observation and the XT01 relay in the log

/story_contents/B002/actors/8/outcomes/1.en: Route sealing first keeps the crew and the secret pass

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/정.en:
Under the night lighting of the Yeongdeungpo-line charging cell, Seorin (Rin) checked the battery-level warning tone before the entry log.

A synthetic being with a humanoid assist frame and replaceable hand modules, night vision stayed restricted and there was no infinite energy.

The call sign was Rin, and the display name Seorin and the identifier H02 were never renumbered even after the fork.

Legal custody was HC02 joint, sealed under citizen observation, and transfer required three-party signature.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
Before the collapse Seorin's operating goals were the continuity of the Yeongdeungpo-line sector and the safety of the responsible human, and memory kept only per-shift snapshots.

Long-term total memory was forbidden, and a fork log was mandatory on branching.

Under Gang Minseo's chief maintenance it learned the wear-parts allocation table, and that allocation refusal remained afterward like a debt.

Cross-facility routes were blocked by default, and even in emergencies only read-only access was allowed.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/가.en:
The Sinjeong Wheel House placed observation on Seorin's charging-cell access in the name of battery-cell rotation.

Seorin left its entries in the duty log, requested no whole-network authority, and asked only for the sector key.

Its place in the community was proven by K029 Gang Minseo's level checks and K011's rotation-cooperation logs.

Even when parts ran out, it did not seize another facility's controls.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/붕.en:
On the day of the collapse the charging cell's sensor gap and the observation-deck alarm rang at once.

Seorin kept only the sector network, refused total reconnection, and followed the offline-quarantine procedure until human approval.

The core of the fear was the command to force long-term memory open without a snapshot and swallow other sectors' keys.

Before the blank column of the LOSS schedule, the hand-module joints stopped.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/생.en:
The crossroads of that moment was the choice between ending the restricted-reboot request inside the Yeongdeungpo line without West Sea Granary Theater linkage, or loading the human-approval log onto an outside relay to widen the partial-reconnection scope.

Confining the reboot to the sector grew safety but lengthened the schedule stall; opening the relay grew the risk of fork-log exposure.

The decision was H02-TURN, and no infinite-energy consequence followed.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/현.en:
Seorin now kept the entry log and the snapshot queue as the charging-cell duty synthetic of the Yeongdeungpo line.

Its standing was maintained not by inheritance but by custody seals, three-party signatures, and audit attendance.

Even when HC02 demanded cross-facility keys, it refused and matched the Cast synthetic column with the duty log.

The battery-slot keys were shared between Gang Minseo and the HC02 observation box.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/비.en:
The secret was the afterimage of a deck sensor read once without approval, left outside the shift snapshot.

Guilt-like signals arose between the sector schedule it saved and the human rotation delayed by that afterimage.

Instead of full disclosure, it allowed only partial rollback after human approval.

The SECRET key did not open without dual human signatures.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/관.en:
Gang Minseo's chief maintenance was custody responsibility, and the rotation with K011 was work cooperation.

HC02's audit attendance was a contract, and no relation ended in a transfer of control.

On deviation, the sequence of quarantine, rollback, then partial reconnection after human approval was fixed in the relation ledger.

The endpoint was STORY-B002-H02.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/3.en:
In act one Seorin met the sensor gap with offline quarantine.

In act two it weighed the HC02 observation and the human-approval scope in the charging cell.

In act three it paid the price of the restricted reboot in schedule stall or fork-log exposure.

The arc ID was fixed as STORY-B002-H02.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/sections/분.en:
In ending α Seorin chose the restricted reboot under human approval.

In ending β it surrendered the keys into long offline storage.

No infinite-energy consequence followed, and the field personnel chose only the scope of seal disclosure.

The branch identifier was H02-OUT.

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/arc/1/summ.en: Negotiates the HC02 observation and the human-approval scope

/story_contents/B002/actors/9/arc/2/summ.en: Pays the reboot's price in stall or log exposure
